    +    p_query text, p_pattern text, p_limit integer DEFAULT 11, p_container_id uuid DEFAULT NULL
    +) RETURNS TABLE (
    +    id uuid, container_id uuid, contributor_id uuid, contributor_name text, note text,
    +    original_amount text, original_currency text, entry_type text, status text,
    +    recorded_at timestamp with time zone, match_type text, score real
    +)
    +    LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY INVOKER
    +    SET search_path TO pg_catalog, public, extensions, pg_temp
    +    SET pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold TO '0.3'
    +    AS $$
    +    WITH actor AS (
    +        SELECT m.id, (coalesce(p_is_admin, false) AND m.role = 'admin') AS is_admin
    +        FROM public.workspace_members m
    +        JOIN public.workspaces w ON w.id = m.workspace_id AND w.deleted_at IS NULL
    +        WHERE m.id = p_caller_id AND m.workspace_id = p_workspace_id
    +          AND m.is_active = true AND m.deleted_at IS NULL AND m.role IN ('member', 'admin')
    +    ), query_amount AS (
    +        -- Cast only a bounded, plain signed decimal. Currency interpretation,
    +        -- conversion and natural-language amount inference are not performed.
    +        SELECT CASE WHEN char_length(p_query) BETWEEN 2 AND 200
    +                         AND p_query ~ '^[+-]?[0-9]+([.][0-9]{1,2})?$'
    +                    THEN p_query::numeric ELSE NULL END AS amount
    +    ), matches AS (
    +        SELECT e.id, e.container_id, e.contributor_id, contributor.display_name AS contributor_name,
    +            e.note, e.original_amount::text AS original_amount, e.original_currency,
    +            e.entry_type, e.status, e.recorded_at,
    +            CASE WHEN e.original_amount = q.amount OR lower(e.note) = lower(p_query)
    +                           OR lower(contributor.display_name) = lower(p_query) THEN 'exact'
    +                 WHEN e.note ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\'
    +                           OR contributor.display_name ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\' THEN 'substring'
    +                 ELSE 'fuzzy' END AS match_type,
    +            greatest(similarity(p_query, e.note), word_similarity(p_query, e.note),
    +                     similarity(p_query, contributor.display_name), word_similarity(p_query, contributor.display_name),
    +                     0::real) AS score
    +        FROM public.ledger_entries e
    +        JOIN public.containers c ON c.id = e.container_id
    +        LEFT JOIN public.workspace_members contributor
    +          ON contributor.id = e.contributor_id AND contributor.workspace_id = p_workspace_id
    +        CROSS JOIN actor a CROSS JOIN query_amount q
    +        WHERE e.workspace_id = p_workspace_id AND c.workspace_id = p_workspace_id AND c.deleted_at IS NULL
    +          AND (a.is_admin OR e.contributor_id = a.id)
    +          AND (p_container_id IS NULL OR e.container_id = p_container_id)
    +          AND char_length(p_query) BETWEEN 2 AND 200
    +          AND (e.original_amount = q.amount
    +               OR e.note ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\'
    +               OR contributor.display_name ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\'
    +               OR (char_length(p_query) >= 3 AND (e.note %> p_query OR contributor.display_name %> p_query)))
    +    )
    +    SELECT m.id, m.container_id, m.contributor_id, m.contributor_name, m.note,
    +           m.original_amount, m.original_currency, m.entry_type, m.status, m.recorded_at, m.match_type, m.score
    +    FROM matches m
    +    ORDER BY CASE m.match_type WHEN 'exact' THEN 0 WHEN 'substring' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END,
    +             m.score DESC, lower(coalesce(m.note, '')) COLLATE "C", m.id
    +    LIMIT least(21, greatest(2, coalesce(p_limit, 11)));
    +$$;
    +
    +CREATE FUNCTION public.search_disputes_ranked(
    +    p_workspace_id uuid, p_caller_id uuid, p_is_admin boolean,
    +    p_query text, p_pattern text, p_limit integer DEFAULT 11
    +) RETURNS TABLE (
    +    id uuid, ledger_entry_id uuid, raised_by uuid, raised_by_name text, reason text,
    +    status text, raised_at timestamp with time zone, match_type text, score real
    +)
    +    LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY INVOKER
    +    SET search_path TO pg_catalog, public, extensions, pg_temp
    +    SET pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold TO '0.3'
    +    AS $$
    +    WITH actor AS (
    +        SELECT m.id, (coalesce(p_is_admin, false) AND m.role = 'admin') AS is_admin
    +        FROM public.workspace_members m
    +        JOIN public.workspaces w ON w.id = m.workspace_id AND w.deleted_at IS NULL
    +        WHERE m.id = p_caller_id AND m.workspace_id = p_workspace_id
    +          AND m.is_active = true AND m.deleted_at IS NULL AND m.role IN ('member', 'admin')
    +    ), matches AS (
    +        SELECT d.id, d.ledger_entry_id, d.raised_by, raiser.display_name AS raised_by_name,
    +            d.reason, d.status, d.raised_at,
    +            CASE WHEN lower(d.reason) = lower(p_query) OR lower(raiser.display_name) = lower(p_query)
    +                           OR lower(e.note) = lower(p_query) THEN 'exact'
    +                 WHEN d.reason ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\' OR raiser.display_name ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\'
    +                           OR e.note ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\' THEN 'substring'
    +                 ELSE 'fuzzy' END AS match_type,
    +            greatest(similarity(p_query, d.reason), word_similarity(p_query, d.reason),
    +                     similarity(p_query, raiser.display_name), word_similarity(p_query, raiser.display_name),
    +                     similarity(p_query, e.note), word_similarity(p_query, e.note), 0::real) AS score
    +        FROM public.disputes d
    +        LEFT JOIN public.workspace_members raiser
    +          ON raiser.id = d.raised_by AND raiser.workspace_id = p_workspace_id
    +        LEFT JOIN public.ledger_entries e
    +          ON e.id = d.ledger_entry_id AND e.workspace_id = p_workspace_id
    +        CROSS JOIN actor a
    +        WHERE d.workspace_id = p_workspace_id AND (a.is_admin OR d.raised_by = a.id)
    +          AND char_length(p_query) BETWEEN 2 AND 200
    +          AND (d.reason ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\' OR raiser.display_name ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\'
    +               OR e.note ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\'
    +               OR (char_length(p_query) >= 3 AND (d.reason %> p_query OR raiser.display_name %> p_query OR e.note %> p_query)))
    +    )
    +    SELECT m.id, m.ledger_entry_id, m.raised_by, m.raised_by_name, m.reason, m.status, m.raised_at, m.match_type, m.score
    +    FROM matches m
    +    ORDER BY CASE m.match_type WHEN 'exact' THEN 0 WHEN 'substring' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END,
    +             m.score DESC, lower(m.reason) COLLATE "C", m.id
    +    LIMIT least(21, greatest(2, coalesce(p_limit, 11)));
    +$$;
    +
    +CREATE FUNCTION public.search_groups_ranked(
    +    p_workspace_id uuid, p_query text, p_pattern text, p_limit integer DEFAULT 11
    +) RETURNS TABLE (id uuid, name text, description text, created_at timestamp with time zone, match_type text, score real)
    +    LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY INVOKER
    +    SET search_path TO pg_catalog, public, extensions, pg_temp
    +    SET pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold TO '0.3'
    +    AS $$
    +    WITH matches AS (
    +        SELECT g.id, g.name, g.description, g.created_at,
    +            CASE WHEN lower(g.name) = lower(p_query) THEN 'exact'
    +                 WHEN g.name ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\' THEN 'substring'
    +                 ELSE 'fuzzy' END AS match_type,
    +            greatest(similarity(p_query, g.name), word_similarity(p_query, g.name)) AS score
    +        FROM public.groups g
    +        WHERE g.workspace_id = p_workspace_id AND char_length(p_query) BETWEEN 2 AND 200
    +          AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.workspaces w WHERE w.id = p_workspace_id AND w.deleted_at IS NULL)
    +          AND (g.name ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\' OR (char_length(p_query) >= 3 AND g.name %> p_query))
    +    )
    +    SELECT m.id, m.name, m.description, m.created_at, m.match_type, m.score
    +    FROM matches m
    +    ORDER BY CASE m.match_type WHEN 'exact' THEN 0 WHEN 'substring' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END,
    +             m.score DESC, lower(m.name) COLLATE "C", m.id
    +    LIMIT least(21, greatest(2, coalesce(p_limit, 11)));
    +$$;
    +
    +REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION
    +    public.search_tasks_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer, uuid),
    +    public.search_ledger_entries_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer, uuid),
    +    public.search_disputes_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer),
    +    public.search_groups_ranked(uuid, text, text, integer) FROM PUBLIC;
    +
    +DO $$
    +DECLARE browser_role text;
    +BEGIN
    +    FOR browser_role IN SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname IN ('anon', 'authenticated') LOOP
    +        EXECUTE format('REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.search_tasks_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer, uuid), public.search_ledger_entries_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer, uuid), public.search_disputes_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer), public.search_groups_ranked(uuid, text, text, integer) FROM %I', browser_role);
    +    END LOOP;
    +    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'service_role') THEN
    +        GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA extensions TO service_role;
    +        GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION
    +            public.search_tasks_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer, uuid),
    +            public.search_ledger_entries_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer, uuid),
    +            public.search_disputes_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer),
    +            public.search_groups_ranked(uuid, text, text, integer) TO service_role;
    +    END IF;
    +END;
    +$$;
    +
     -- =====================================================================
     -- NOTIFICATIONS
     -- =====================================================================

    jest.mock('../../../src/services/search.service', () => ({
      findMembers: jest.fn(),
      findContainers: jest.fn(),
    }));
    jest.mock('../../../src/services/dashboard.service', () => ({
      getDashboardData: jest.fn(),
      getOverdueSummaryData: jest.fn(),
    }));
    
    const searchService = require('../../../src/services/search.service');
    const { findMember, findContainer } = require('../../../src/agent/services/resolution-tools.service');
    const { getAvailableTools, executeReadTool } = require('../../../src/agent/services/tool-registry.service');
    const { ForbiddenError, ValidationError, AppError } = require('../../../src/utils/errors');
    
    function makeContext(role = 'member') {
      return {
        userId: '11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111',
        member: {
          id: '22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222', role, displayName: 'Adaeze',
          isProxy: false, isActive: true, workspaceId: '33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333',
        },
        workspace: { id: '33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333', name: 'Family', baseCurrency: 'NGN' },
      };
    }
    
    describe.each([
      ['find_member', findMember, searchService.findMembers],
      ['find_container', findContainer, searchService.findContainers],
    ])('%s resolution tool', (name, handler, service) => {
      beforeEach(() => service.mockReset());
    
      it.each(['member', 'admin'])('is a Tier 0 tool available to an authenticated %s', async (role) => {
        const context = makeContext(role);
        expect(getAvailableTools(context).find((tool) => tool.name === name)).toMatchObject({ tier: 0, minRole: 'member' });
        service.mockResolvedValue({ query: 'Adaeze', status: 'not_found', candidates: [], has_more: false });
        await executeReadTool({ name, args: { query: '  Adaeze  ' }, context });
        expect(service).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ workspaceId: context.workspace.id, query: 'Adaeze', limit: 10 });
      });
    
      it.each(['not_found', 'single_match', 'ambiguous'])('preserves the %s result without choosing a candidate', async (status) => {
        const candidates = status === 'not_found' ? [] : [{ id: 'candidate-a', score: 0.5 }];
        if (status === 'ambiguous') candidates.push({ id: 'candidate-b', score: 0.4 });
        const payload = { query: 'Adaze', status, candidates, has_more: false };
        service.mockResolvedValue(payload);
        const result = await executeReadTool({ name, args: { query: 'Adaze' }, context: makeContext() });
        expect(result).toBe(payload);
        expect(result).not.toHaveProperty('resolved_id');
      });
    
      it.each([
        null,
        { ...makeContext(), member: { ...makeContext().member, role: 'owner' } },
        { ...makeContext(), member: { ...makeContext().member, isActive: false } },
        { ...makeContext(), workspace: { id: 'another-workspace' } },
      ])('denies an invalid context even when calling the handler directly', async (context) => {
        await expect(handler({ args: { query: 'Adaeze' }, context })).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(ForbiddenError);
        expect(service).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      });
    
      it.each([
        { workspace_id: 'another-workspace' }, { workspaceId: 'another-workspace' },
        { isAdmin: true }, { role: 'admin' }, { query: '' }, { query: 'a' }, { query: 'a'.repeat(201) },
        { limit: 1 }, { limit: 21 }, { limit: '10' },
      ])('rejects malformed or forged arguments: %j', async (override) => {
        await expect(executeReadTool({ name, args: { query: 'Adaeze', ...override }, context: makeContext() }))
          .rejects.toBeInstanceOf(ValidationError);
        expect(service).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      });
    
      it('always supplies the server workspace even if a direct caller includes a different one', async () => {
        const context = makeContext();
        await handler({ args: { query: 'Adaeze', workspaceId: 'another-workspace', limit: 2 }, context });
        expect(service).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ workspaceId: context.workspace.id, query: 'Adaeze', limit: 2 });
      });
    
      it('preserves service errors rather than inventing an empty candidate list', async () => {
        const error = new AppError('Search unavailable', 503, 'SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE');
        service.mockRejectedValue(error);
        await expect(executeReadTool({ name, args: { query: 'Adaeze' }, context: makeContext() })).rejects.toBe(error);
      });
    });

      const { mockSupabase } = require('../../mocks/supabase.mock');

    const { findMembers, findContainers } = require('../../../src/services/search.service');
    const db = require('../../../src/config/supabase').__mockInstance;
    const { ValidationError } = require('../../../src/utils/errors');
    
    const workspaceId = '11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111';
    const member = {
      id: '22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222', display_name: 'Adaeze Okafor',
      role: 'member', is_proxy: true, match_type: 'fuzzy', score: 0.5,
    };
    const container = {
      id: '33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333', name: 'Rent',
      container_type: 'recurring', status: 'active', match_type: 'exact', score: 1,
    };
    
    describe.each([
      ['members', findMembers, 'search_members_ranked', member],
      ['containers', findContainers, 'search_containers_ranked', container],
    ])('ranked %s search', (label, find, rpcName, candidate) => {
      beforeEach(() => db.reset());
    
      it('scopes the RPC, trims the query, escapes wildcards, and requests a lookahead row', async () => {
        db.mockNextRpcResponse({ data: [], error: null });
        const result = await find({ workspaceId, query: '  50%_x\\  ' });
    
        expect(db.getRpcCalls()).toEqual([{
          fnName: rpcName,
          params: { p_workspace_id: workspaceId, p_query: '50%_x\\', p_pattern: '%50\\%\\_x\\\\%', p_limit: 11 },
        }]);
        expect(result).toEqual({ query: '50%_x\\', status: 'not_found', candidates: [], has_more: false });
      });
    
      it('returns a single candidate with only allowed fields and its original score', async () => {
        db.mockNextRpcResponse({ data: [{ ...candidate, admin_notes: 'secret', public_token: 'secret' }], error: null });
        const result = await find({ workspaceId, query: 'Adaze' });
    
        expect(result).toEqual({ query: 'Adaze', status: 'single_match', candidates: [candidate], has_more: false });
        expect(result).not.toHaveProperty('resolved_id');
      });
    
      it('preserves database ranking and marks multiple candidates ambiguous even with an exact first result', async () => {
        const first = { ...candidate, match_type: 'exact', score: 1 };
        const second = { ...candidate, id: '44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444', match_type: 'fuzzy', score: 0.4 };
        db.mockNextRpcResponse({ data: [first, second], error: null });
    
        await expect(find({ workspaceId, query: 'Adaeze', limit: 2 })).resolves.toEqual({
          query: 'Adaeze', status: 'ambiguous', candidates: [first, second], has_more: false,
        });
      });
    
      it('truncates the display list without hiding additional candidates', async () => {
        const rows = Array.from({ length: 3 }, (_, index) => ({ ...candidate, id: `candidate-${index}` }));
        db.mockNextRpcResponse({ data: rows, error: null });
        const result = await find({ workspaceId, query: 'Adaeze', limit: 2 });
    
        expect(result).toEqual({ query: 'Adaeze', status: 'ambiguous', candidates: rows.slice(0, 2), has_more: true });
        expect(db.getRpcCalls()[0].params.p_limit).toBe(3);
      });
    
      it.each([
        { query: '' }, { query: '   ' }, { query: 'a' }, { query: null }, { query: 123 },
        { query: 'a'.repeat(201) }, { limit: 1 }, { limit: 21 }, { limit: 2.5 }, { limit: '10' },
        { workspaceId: 'invalid' }, { workspaceId: undefined },
      ])('rejects invalid parameters before reaching the database: %j', async (override) => {
        await expect(find({ workspaceId, query: 'Adaeze', ...override })).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(ValidationError);
        expect(db.getRpcCalls()).toEqual([]);
      });
    
      it.each([
        { data: null, error: { code: 'PGRST202', message: 'RPC missing with internal details' } },
        { data: null, error: null },
        { data: {}, error: null },
      ])('reports an unavailable search instead of a false no-match on RPC failure', async (response) => {
        db.mockNextRpcResponse(response);
        await expect(find({ workspaceId, query: 'Adaeze' })).rejects.toMatchObject({
          statusCode: 503, code: 'SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE', message: 'Entity search is unavailable. Please try again.',
        });
      });
    
      it('converts transport failures into the same typed availability error', async () => {
        db.client.rpc.mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('Network detail'));
        await expect(find({ workspaceId, query: 'Adaeze' })).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE' });
      });
    });

    // Requires the real Postgres/PostgREST/Redis test stack with 001_schema.sql
    // applied. Unit mocks cannot validate trigram operators, indexes, or SQL scope.
    const { Pool } = require('pg');
    const { supabaseAdmin } = require('../../../src/config/supabase');
    const { containsPattern } = require('../../../src/utils/ilike');
    const { seedWorkspaceWithAdmin, cleanupWorkspace } = require('../../helpers/dbHelper');
    const { buildProxyMember, buildContainer } = require('../../fixtures/factories');
    
    describe('ranked entity search RPCs with Postgres', () => {
      const workspaceIds = [];
    
      async function search(rpcName, { workspaceId, query, limit = 11 }) {
        const { data, error } = await supabaseAdmin.rpc(rpcName, {
          p_workspace_id: workspaceId, p_query: query, p_pattern: containsPattern(query), p_limit: limit,
        });
        if (error) throw error;
        return data;
      }
    
      const searchMembers = (params) => search('search_members_ranked', params);
      const searchContainers = (params) => search('search_containers_ranked', params);
    
      async function seedTenant() {
        const tenant = await seedWorkspaceWithAdmin(supabaseAdmin, { member: { display_name: 'Xylophone' } });
        workspaceIds.push(tenant.workspace.id);
        return tenant;
      }
    
      async function addMember(workspaceId, name, overrides = {}) {
        const { data, error } = await supabaseAdmin.from('workspace_members').insert(buildProxyMember({
          workspace_id: workspaceId, display_name: name, ...overrides,
        })).select().single();
        if (error) throw error;
        return data;
      }
    
      async function addContainer(tenant, name, overrides = {}) {
        const { data, error } = await supabaseAdmin.from('containers').insert(buildContainer({
          workspace_id: tenant.workspace.id, created_by: tenant.member.id, name, ...overrides,
        })).select().single();
        if (error) throw error;
        return data;
      }
    
      afterAll(async () => {
        for (const workspaceId of workspaceIds) await cleanupWorkspace(supabaseAdmin, workspaceId);
      });
    
      it('finds a misspelled first name within a full member name', async () => {
        const { workspace } = await seedTenant();
        const member = await addMember(workspace.id, 'Adaeze Okafor');
        const result = await searchMembers({ workspaceId: workspace.id, query: 'Adaze' });
        expect(result).toEqual([expect.objectContaining({ id: member.id, match_type: 'fuzzy', is_proxy: true })]);
        expect(result[0].score).toBeGreaterThan(0.3);
        expect(result[0].score).toBeLessThan(1);
      });
    
      it('ranks exact names before substrings before fuzzy matches, returning all candidates', async () => {
        const { workspace } = await seedTenant();
        const fuzzy = await addMember(workspace.id, 'Adaze');
        const substring = await addMember(workspace.id, 'Adaeze Okafor');
        const exact = await addMember(workspace.id, 'Adaeze');
        const result = await searchMembers({ workspaceId: workspace.id, query: 'adaeze' });
        expect(result.map((candidate) => candidate.id)).toEqual([exact.id, substring.id, fuzzy.id]);
        expect(result.map((candidate) => candidate.match_type)).toEqual(['exact', 'substring', 'fuzzy']);
      });
    
      it('excludes inactive, deleted, and other-workspace members', async () => {
        const first = await seedTenant();
        const second = await seedTenant();
        const active = await addMember(first.workspace.id, 'Adaeze');
        await addMember(first.workspace.id, 'Adaeze', { is_active: false });
        await addMember(first.workspace.id, 'Adaeze', { deleted_at: new Date().toISOString() });
        await addMember(second.workspace.id, 'Adaeze');
        const result = await searchMembers({ workspaceId: first.workspace.id, query: 'Adaeze' });
        expect(result.map((candidate) => candidate.id)).toEqual([active.id]);
      });
    
      it('uses a deterministic order for duplicate names when limiting results', async () => {
        const { workspace } = await seedTenant();
        const members = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) members.push(await addMember(workspace.id, 'Adaeze'));
        const result = await searchMembers({ workspaceId: workspace.id, query: 'Adaeze', limit: 2 });
        expect(result.map((candidate) => candidate.id)).toEqual(members.map((member) => member.id).sort().slice(0, 2));
      });
    
      it('finds typo matches in container names and preserves exact-match priority', async () => {
        const tenant = await seedTenant();
        const fuzzy = await addContainer(tenant, 'Adaeze rent pool');
        const exact = await addContainer(tenant, 'Adaze');
        const result = await searchContainers({ workspaceId: tenant.workspace.id, query: 'Adaze' });
        expect(result.map((candidate) => candidate.id)).toEqual([exact.id, fuzzy.id]);
        expect(result[1].match_type).toBe('fuzzy');
      });
    
      it('includes archived containers but excludes deleted and other-workspace containers', async () => {
        const first = await seedTenant();
        const second = await seedTenant();
        const archived = await addContainer(first, 'Rent', { status: 'archived' });
        await addContainer(first, 'Rent', { deleted_at: new Date().toISOString() });
        await addContainer(second, 'Rent');
        const result = await searchContainers({ workspaceId: first.workspace.id, query: 'Rent' });
        expect(result).toEqual([expect.objectContaining({ id: archived.id, status: 'archived' })]);
      });

    # Ranked search extension proposal
    
    Status: ready for a schema decision; not applied to `migrations/001_schema.sql`.
    
    The remaining Tier 0 tools need the same ranked PostgreSQL search already
    used by `find_member` and `find_container`. This proposal adds four read-only
    RPCs and four indexes to the consolidated schema. It reuses the installed
    `pg_trgm` extension, `search.service.js`, `containsPattern()`, and the existing
    candidate/disambiguation contract. It introduces no tables or dependencies.
    
    ## Functions and permissions
    
    | Tool | RPC | Member visibility | Admin visibility |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | `find_tasks` | `search_tasks_ranked` | Tasks assigned to the caller | Tasks in the current workspace |
    | `find_ledger_entries` | `search_ledger_entries_ranked` | Entries whose contributor is the caller | Entries in the current workspace |
    | `find_disputes` | `search_disputes_ranked` | Disputes raised by the caller | Disputes in the current workspace |
    | `find_group` | `search_groups_ranked` | Group directory metadata | Group directory metadata |
    
    All handlers explicitly require active membership before calling the search
    service. Workspace/caller IDs and the real admin flag come only from server
    context. Strict model argument schemas cannot override them. Group search
    follows the member-visible list route; `get_group` remains admin-only.
    
    Tasks and ledger entries must belong to a non-deleted container in the
    authenticated workspace. Tasks must also be non-deleted. Ledger rows must
    match the workspace both directly and through their parent container.
    Dispute search follows `get_dispute`: it can find historical disputes even
    when a related container has been deleted. Joined member/ledger rows are
    scoped to the same workspace. All searches exclude deleted workspaces.
    
    For the three private-data RPCs, a scoped lookup of the caller's current
    membership additionally requires `is_active = true` and `deleted_at IS NULL`.
    The SQL admin branch requires both the server-supplied admin flag and an
    actual `admin` role on that membership. Missing/inactive/mismatched membership
    returns no candidates. This is an explicit query boundary; it does not rely
    on RLS.
    
    Proposed signatures:
    
    ```sql
    search_tasks_ranked(
      p_workspace_id uuid, p_caller_id uuid, p_is_admin boolean,
      p_query text, p_pattern text, p_limit integer DEFAULT 11,
      p_container_id uuid DEFAULT NULL
    )
    
    search_ledger_entries_ranked(
      p_workspace_id uuid, p_caller_id uuid, p_is_admin boolean,
      p_query text, p_pattern text, p_limit integer DEFAULT 11,
      p_container_id uuid DEFAULT NULL
    )
    
    search_disputes_ranked(
      p_workspace_id uuid, p_caller_id uuid, p_is_admin boolean,
      p_query text, p_pattern text, p_limit integer DEFAULT 11
    )
    
    search_groups_ranked(
      p_workspace_id uuid, p_query text, p_pattern text,
      p_limit integer DEFAULT 11
    )
    ```
    
    Functions use `LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY INVOKER`, the existing pinned
    `pg_catalog, public, extensions, pg_temp` search path and a word-similarity
    threshold of `0.3`. Execution is revoked from `PUBLIC`, `anon` and
    `authenticated`, and granted to `service_role` when that role exists, matching
    the current ranked-search RPCs. Handlers remain the required authorization
    boundary before these service calls.
    
    ## Matching and returned fields
    
    - Tasks: match the title. Candidates contain ID, container ID, title,
      assignee membership ID, stored status and due date.
    - Ledger entries: match note text, contributor name, or an exact original
      amount. A plain signed decimal query is compared as PostgreSQL `numeric`;
      no currency conversion, summation or natural-language amount inference is
      performed. Different currencies can produce separate candidates. Return
      ID, container ID, contributor membership ID/name, note, original amount as
      decimal text, original currency, entry type, stored status and recorded time.
    - Disputes: match the reason, raiser name or linked ledger note. Return ID,
      linked entry ID, raiser membership ID/name, reason, stored status and raised
      time. Notes arrays, proofs and internal ledger fields are not returned.
    - Groups: match the name. Return ID, name, description and creation time.
    
    Every candidate also includes the database `match_type` (`exact`, `substring`
    or `fuzzy`) and original `score`. Rank exact matches first, then escaped
    literal substring matches, then trigram matches; break ties by score, stable
    text ordering and ID. Trigram matching requires at least three query
    characters, matching the current search functions.
    
    Model queries are trimmed and limited to 2–200 characters. Display limits
    are 2–20 with a default of 10; SQL allows at most 21 rows so the service can
    detect `has_more`. Optional `container_id` filters are supported for task and
    ledger searches. The service returns `not_found`, `single_match` or
    `ambiguous` before truncating the candidate list. It never selects a resolved
    ID or treats an exact first result as proof of uniqueness.
    
    All returned names, notes, reasons and descriptions remain untrusted tool
    data. Query failures return `SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE`, never a fabricated
    no-match result. No export or write action is added by this extension.
    
    ## Indexes and insertion point
    
    Add these indexes with the new functions after the `disputes` table and its
    indexes, where all referenced tables exist:
    
    ```sql
    CREATE INDEX idx_tasks_title_trgm ON public.container_tasks
      USING gin (title gin_trgm_ops) WHERE (deleted_at IS NULL);
    
    CREATE INDEX idx_ledger_note_trgm ON public.ledger_entries
      USING gin (note gin_trgm_ops) WHERE (note IS NOT NULL);
    
    CREATE INDEX idx_disputes_reason_trgm ON public.disputes
      USING gin (reason gin_trgm_ops);
    
    CREATE INDEX idx_groups_name_trgm ON public.groups
      USING gin (name gin_trgm_ops);
    ```
    
    Contributor/raiser names reuse the existing member-name trigram index where
    the planner can use it; no duplicate member index is proposed. The consolidated
    schema remains the sole schema source, with no incremental migration runner.
    
    ## Implementation and validation after the decision
    
    Extend `search.service.js` without changing existing search method contracts,
    add strict tool/request validators, and register the four Tier 0 handlers.
    Unit tests cover role/context rejection, the real caller passed to each RPC,
    amount preservation, field trimming, ambiguous results, lookahead, query
    failures and hostile text. Existing chat/provider tool-list tests are updated.
    
    Add real database cases beside `tests/integration/database/ranked-search.test.js`
    for typo ranking, literal wildcard escaping, exact decimal matching, other
    workspaces, private ownership boundaries, stale admin flags, deleted records,
    optional container filters, RPC grants and bounded results. These integration
    tests require the local Postgres/Redis/PostgREST stack and remain pending until
    that stack is available; unit mocks cannot verify SQL authorization or plans.
    # Agent tools
    
    This module currently provides read tools through `getAvailableTools(context)`
    and `executeReadTool({ name, args, context })`. Server code must build context
    after the existing auth and membership middleware:
    
    ```js
    const context = { userId: req.user.id, member: req.member, workspace: req.workspace, requestId: req.requestId };
    ```
    
    The registry includes all 28 Tier 1 tool names from the architecture, with
    the role restrictions and data limits documented below. Tier 0 currently
    includes caller context and ranked member/container lookup. The remaining
    ranked task, ledger, dispute and group searches are specified in the
    [schema proposal](SEARCH_SCHEMA_PROPOSAL.md), pending a schema decision.
    Proposal approval/execution, streaming chat and voice are still pending.
    
    `find_member` and `find_container` take `{ query, limit? }`. Queries are trimmed
    and must contain 2–200 characters; limits default to 10 and range from 2 to 20.
    Workspace and actor IDs are always supplied by server context.
    
    Results contain `query`, `status`, `candidates`, and `has_more`. Candidates are
    ranked in PostgreSQL: exact names, literal substrings, then trigram matches,
    with score/name/ID tie-breakers. `score` is a similarity value, not a probability.
    Members must be active and not deleted; containers may be archived/completed
    but must not be deleted. Both searches exclude deleted workspaces.
    
    - `not_found`: no candidates.
    - `single_match`: one candidate to confirm with the user before a write.
    - `ambiguous`: multiple candidates; the user must choose or refine the query.
    
    No result contains an automatically resolved ID. A future proposal executor
    must enforce the user's entity selection separately from action approval.
    `has_more` means further candidates were omitted; refine the query or increase
    the limit. User-supplied names remain untrusted data.
    
    ## Container browsing
    
    `list_containers` and `get_container` are Tier 1 reads available to active
    members and admins, matching the existing container HTTP routes. Both use
    the authenticated workspace and exclude deleted containers. Handlers check
    membership themselves; model arguments cannot change identity, include
    deleted records, or select a broader service view.
    
    Lists accept optional `type` (`event` or `recurring`), stored `status`
    (`active`, `completed`, or `archived`), and `sort` (`created_at`, `name`, or
    `event_date`, with an optional leading `-` for descending order). The default
    is ascending creation date with an ID tie-breaker. `page` ranges from 1 to
    10,000 and `per_page` from 1 to 100 (defaults: 1 and 20). Filtered totals and
    `next_page` come from the server; the model must not count list rows. A null
    next page means the end of the results or the page limit.
    
    List results contain identity/type/status, subtitle, task/money enablement,
    stored event/recurrence dates, and lifecycle timestamps. `get_container`
    accepts only a resolved `container_id` UUID and adds description, event type,
    recurrence settings, the stored budget target/currency, completion notes,
    and the source container ID after a conversion. Budget targets are settings,
    not collected/remaining balances; the agent must not calculate totals or
    future billing dates. Use `get_container_summary` for permitted financial
    and participant summaries and `list_cycles` for admin billing schedules.
    
    Use `find_container` for names and clarify ambiguous matches. A partial list
    cannot establish that a name is unique. All user-written text remains in the
    untrusted-data envelope. Neither tool exposes public-link tokens, files,
    ledger rows, participant/cycle records, or internal actor fields.
    
    The existing container service supports internal paginated metadata lists
    and a `metadataOnly` detail view, avoiding those unrelated joins and reads.
    Existing HTTP callers keep their unpaginated list/detail envelopes. Failed
    base queries, unavailable list rows, and invalid exact counts return typed
    `CONTAINERS_UNAVAILABLE` errors instead of zero/empty results. A missing

    ## Ledger entry reads
    
    `list_ledger_entries` and `get_ledger_entry` are Tier 1 reads. Members see only
    their own contributor entries; admins see all entries in the container. The
    handlers check active membership and pass the real workspace, member, and
    role. A member's filter targeting another contributor is rejected up front.

    must be ordered; dates without times are rejected. Default order is newest
    first, with an ID tie-breaker. Pagination counts the visible filtered entries
    and supplies `next_page`. This is not a filtered financial-total tool; the
    model must not sum entries or convert currencies. Cycle filters are not
    supported. Entry details accept only `container_id` and `entry_id`.
    
    Resolve container and contributor names with the existing search tools and
    use list results for entry IDs. Clarify ambiguous entries; a partial page
    cannot establish uniqueness. Both tools return stored amounts verbatim and
    identify the authenticated workspace's base currency. Proof files, storage
    paths, idempotency keys, and internal recorder/confirmer fields are omitted.
    Notes remain untrusted data. No confirmation, correction, export, or write
    operation is exposed by these tools.

    `LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE` instead of reporting empty or zero results. Existing

    scope, ownership, filters, precision, errors, and hostile content. Live
    database isolation and model evaluation remain pending.
    
    ## Notification reads
    
    `list_notifications` and `get_unread_count` read only the caller's own inbox
    in the authenticated workspace, including for admins. Both handlers check
    membership, reject recipient/workspace overrides, and wrap the existing
    notification inbox service. Listing accepts optional boolean `is_read`,
    `page` (1–10,000), and `per_page` (1–100). Counting accepts only `{}`.
    
    Lists return permitted notification text/reference fields and read timestamps,
    omitting delivery internals and deduplication keys. Results include filtered
    pagination with `next_page`; `unread_count` covers all unread notifications in
    this workspace, independent of the list filter or page. Reading does not mark
    anything as read. Notification titles/bodies remain untrusted tool content.
    
    The inbox service now applies the same recipient/workspace scope to the list
    and unread counter, uses stable creation-date/ID ordering, and rejects query
    failures or unavailable counts with `NOTIFICATIONS_UNAVAILABLE`. Existing
    HTTP read controllers use the workspace from the resolved membership and
    keep their existing response envelopes. Mocked service, tool, loop, and HTTP
    tests cover these boundaries; live database/model verification remains pending.
    
    ## Group reads
    
    `list_groups({ search?, page?, per_page? })` is a Tier 1 read available to
    members and admins. It returns group metadata (ID, name, description and
    timestamps) and an exact filtered group count. Search is an escaped literal
    name substring, 2–200 characters; it does not resolve spelling errors. Groups
    are ordered by name then ID. Embedded memberships and membership counts are
    omitted from this list.
    
    `get_group({ group_id, page?, per_page? })` is **admin-only**, matching the
    existing group-detail HTTP route. It returns group metadata, a bounded page
    of membership directory fields and an exact membership count. Both the group
    and the joined memberships are scoped to the authenticated workspace. Deleted
    members are excluded; proxies and inactive memberships remain visible.
    Members are ordered by added timestamp then group-membership ID. No contact
    information, actor IDs, or financial details are exposed.
    
    Both tools use pages 1–10,000 and 1–100 rows per page (defaults 1/20), with
    `pagination.next_page` null at the last page or page limit. Group detail
    pagination describes memberships, while list pagination describes groups.
    Use the service count; never infer totals or name uniqueness from page length.
    Duplicate group names require clarification. Descriptions and relationship
    text remain in untrusted tool-result envelopes. Missing groups return
    `NOT_FOUND`; failed queries or unavailable exact counts return
    `GROUPS_UNAVAILABLE`. Internal pagination options preserve the legacy HTTP
    response shapes. Live PostgREST join/count validation remains pending.
    
    ## Dispute reads
    
    `list_disputes({ status?, page?, per_page? })` is admin-only. It lists disputes
    by newest raised timestamp then ID, with an optional `open`/`resolved` filter.
    The exact count covers matching disputes, including those whose linked entry
    is unavailable. Results include stored entry amounts but omit embedded notes.
    
    `get_dispute({ dispute_id, page?, per_page? })` is available to admins and to
    the member who raised that dispute. The handler checks membership, forwards
    the real caller and role, and verifies ownership before returning the result.
    The service checks ownership before reading the linked entry. Every parent
    and related-record lookup stays in the authenticated workspace. A missing
    linked entry is `null`; a failed query is an error.
    
    Detail pagination applies to notes in stored append order, using
    `notes_pagination`; its total is the service-counted length of the stored
    notes array. Both tools default to page 1/20, allow pages 1–10,000 and 1–100
    rows per page, and return a null `next_page` at the last page or page limit.
    Smaller pages may be needed for long text to fit the shared tool-result limit.
    IDs can come from notifications or an admin dispute list; ambiguous references
    need clarification. Reasons, resolutions, notes and linked-entry text remain
    untrusted data. Stored monetary precision/currency is preserved, with the
    workspace base currency supplied by server context. No proof paths,
    idempotency keys, or dispute writes are exposed.
    
    Internal metadata and note-pagination options preserve legacy HTTP response
    shapes. Failed queries, invalid list counts or malformed notes fail with
    `DISPUTES_UNAVAILABLE`. Unit coverage includes the ownership and workspace
    boundaries; live PostgREST join validation remains pending.
    
    ## Invite and audit reads
    
    `list_invites({ status?, page?, per_page? })` is admin-only. It returns invite
    IDs, inviter directory names/IDs, stored timestamps, service-evaluated status
    and an exact filtered count. Optional status is `available`, `used` or
    `expired`. The service uses one `as_of` timestamp for filtering and status;
    used takes precedence over expiry, and the expiry boundary matches the
    existing preview service. Revoked invites are deleted and absent from results.
    Invite tokens, URLs and recipient account IDs are excluded. This read cannot
    create, accept, revoke or send an invite.
    
    `get_audit_log({ action?, actor_member_id?, from?, to?, page?, per_page? })`
    is admin-only. Action filters come from the frozen `AUDIT_ACTIONS` catalog;
    actor filtering uses a resolved membership ID and never changes the caller.
    Date bounds are inclusive ISO timestamps with explicit timezones. Results
    contain only event IDs/actions, actor membership IDs/names, target types/IDs
    and timestamps. An unavailable actor display name is `null`; it must not be
    used to infer a person or attribute an event to System. Raw audit metadata,
    account IDs, IP addresses and user-agent fields are excluded. CSV export
    remains outside the registry.
    
    Both tools use newest timestamp then ID ordering, default page 1/20, pages
    1–10,000 and 1–100 rows per page. Exact counts cover the requested filters;
    `next_page` is null at the last page or page limit. Service failures and invalid
    counts return `INVITES_UNAVAILABLE` or `AUDIT_LOG_UNAVAILABLE`. Names remain
    untrusted data. Internal service options retain legacy HTTP response shapes.
    Unit coverage verifies role checks, field trimming, filtering, expiry states,
    count failures and prompt-injection handling. Live join/count validation is
    still pending.
    
    ## Participant and target reads
    
    `list_participants({ container_id, page?, per_page? })`,
    `get_target_history({ container_id, participant_id, page?, per_page? })` and
    `get_cycle_targets({ container_id, participant_id, page?, per_page? })` are
    all admin-only, matching the nested participant HTTP routes. Each handler
    enforces that gate before calling the participant service, which trusts its
    caller. Model arguments cannot supply identity, role or internal service
    options. Container and participant lookups verify the authenticated workspace
    and exclude deleted containers/memberships; proxies and inactive memberships
    remain visible.
    
    The participant list includes directory/tracking fields and the stored current
    non-cycle target, ordered by added timestamp then participant ID. The exact
    count describes visible participants. Only current targets for that page are
    fetched; missing targets have no invented zero amount. Participant notes and
    internal actor/public-visibility fields are excluded.
    
    Target history includes cycle and non-cycle versions, original amount/currency,
    current and supersession state, and setter directory IDs/names. It is ordered
    by newest set timestamp then target ID; its count describes matching versions.
    Use the participant **record ID** from `list_participants`, not the distinct
    `workspace_member_id`. Duplicate names require clarification.
    
    Cycle-target pages are ordered by cycle number and include every returned
    cycle, with its current stored target or `null`. Their exact count describes
    cycles. They return stored schedule and original-currency target fields only.
    The legacy service compares base-currency payments to original-currency
    targets and sums an unbounded ledger query; those payment totals and
    classifications are omitted from agent results. A null target does not establish
    skipped/paid/overdue participant status. Existing summary tools retain their
    documented financial scopes.
    
    Defaults are page 1/20, with pages 1–10,000 and 1–100 rows per page. All results
    include bounded `next_page` continuation. Failed reads, invalid counts or
    duplicate/mismatched current targets return `PARTICIPANTS_UNAVAILABLE`;
    missing scoped resources return `NOT_FOUND`. Untrusted labels/setter names
    stay in tool-result envelopes. Opt-in pagination preserves legacy HTTP behavior.
    Unit coverage verifies role/scoping branches, monetary preservation, count
    failures, duplicate-name clarification and exclusion of writes. Live PostgREST
    join/count validation remains pending.
    
    ## Timeline and milestone reads
    
    `get_timeline({ limit?, cursor? })` and `get_milestone({ milestone_id })` are
    available to active members and admins. Both use the authenticated workspace
    and exclude deleted records. Timeline items contain milestone metadata and
    dated container completions; file paths/photos are excluded. The timeline
    limit defaults to 20 and ranges from 1 to 100. It provides continuation and
    has no workspace total count.
    
    To continue, copy the complete returned `next_cursor` object into `cursor`:
    
    ```json
    {
      "limit": 20,
      "cursor": {
        "before_container": { "date": "2026-11-01T12:00:00.000Z", "id": "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111" },
        "before_milestone": null
      }
    }
    ```
    
    Both source keys are required when a cursor is supplied. Container cursor
    dates are ISO timestamps with explicit timezones; milestone cursor dates are
    `YYYY-MM-DD`. IDs are UUIDs. Null source cursors mean that source has not
    advanced. Sources are ordered by descending date and ascending ID; merged
    items preserve source ordering, including sub-millisecond completion dates.
    Container completions precede milestones at equal instants. Each source uses
    one lookahead row, and cursors advance only past items actually returned.
    Date-and-ID cursors prevent same-date events from being skipped. At the end,
    `has_more` is false and `next_cursor` is null.
    
    Milestone details contain title, description, date, type and timestamps.
    Use timeline `reference_type`/`reference_id` to choose `get_milestone` or
    `get_container`, and clarify duplicate titles. User text stays untrusted.
    Strict cursor schemas prevent raw filter expressions from reaching the query.
    Failed timeline reads return `TIMELINE_UNAVAILABLE`; detail read failures
    return `MILESTONES_UNAVAILABLE`, and missing milestones return `NOT_FOUND`.
    The internal metadata path preserves legacy HTTP timeline cursor/response
    shapes. Unit tests cover role checks, fields, duplicate-title clarification,
    same-date continuation, source exhaustion and hostile text. Live pagination
    validation remains pending.
    
    ## Chat endpoint
    
    `POST /v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/agent/chat` accepts a bearer token and a JSON
    body containing a nonempty `message` (up to 8,000 characters), with an optional
    `conversation_id` as described below:
    
    ```json
    { "message": "Show my workspace dashboard." }
    ```
    
    This first HTTP increment returns one complete JSON response using the existing
    API envelope. For example, after a dashboard read:
    
    ```json
    {
      "data": {
        "text": "Here is your workspace dashboard.",
        "modelCalls": 2,
        "toolCalls": 2
      }
    }
    ```
    
    `modelCalls` and `toolCalls` are server-counted turn metrics; the initial
    context read is included in `toolCalls`. Successful replies use
    `Cache-Control: no-store`. Omitting `conversation_id` keeps the existing
    stateless behavior and response shape. Streaming remains a later increment.
    
    The route inherits `requireAuth` → `loadDbUser` → `requireMembership` from the
    workspace router. Context comes exclusively from those middleware results.
    Client-supplied history, roles, tools, identity fields, model settings, and
    workspace IDs in the body are rejected. Query parameters cannot change the
    workspace or actor. The tools offered and executed are still role-filtered
    Tier 0/1 reads; chat does not execute writes or approve proposals.
    
    The dedicated `agentLimiter` allows 10 requests per minute per authenticated
    user across all workspaces, using the shared Redis store with prefix
    `rl:agent:`. Existing general limits also apply. A blocked request returns
    429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After` before invoking Groq. The agent and both
    general limiters keep local counters for fallback if Redis commands fail or
    exceed their one-second deadline. Those fallback counts are per process, not
    shared across instances. Missing clients also use memory stores. Membership
    and dashboard cache reads have the same bounded wait and fall back to database
    reads; authentication and membership checks still apply during an outage.
    The shared workspace token budget below is separate from request throttling.
    
    Validation failures return 400; malformed JSON also returns 400 without echoing
    the body, and the application's 1 MiB body limit returns 413. Missing/invalid
    authentication or an unavailable user profile returns 401. An unavailable
    workspace or membership returns the existing non-enumerating 404. Provider
    configuration/unavailability/rate limits return 503, timeouts return 504,
    invalid or truncated completions return 502, and loop/size limits return 422.
    Workspace token exhaustion returns 429 `AGENT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` with
    `Retry-After`; a request exceeding the whole allowance returns 422
    `AGENT_BUDGET_REQUEST_TOO_LARGE`. Invalid budget configuration returns 503.
    Errors use the existing `{ error: { code, message, ... } }` API envelope.
    
    Provider construction happens per accepted request, so missing Groq settings
    disable chat with a 503 without preventing the rest of the API from starting.
    HTTP unit tests run the real application middleware, read loop, and adapter
    with mocked external services. Throttling tests exercise the memory fallback;
    shared Redis enforcement and deployed Supabase/Groq behavior still need live
    integration verification.
    
    ## Conversation continuity
    
    Conversation history is opt-in and owned by the server:
    
    ```json
    { "message": "Show the rent summary.", "conversation_id": null }
    ```
    
    A successful first reply includes `data.conversation_id`, a server-generated
    UUID. Send that ID with a follow-up to resume the conversation:
    
    ```json
    { "message": "The London one.", "conversation_id": "<returned-uuid>" }
    ```
    
    Send `null` again to start over, or omit the field for a stateless request.
    Client-supplied messages/history, tool results, roles, and identity overrides
    remain rejected. The response contains only text, turn metrics, and the ID;
    the saved transcript is never returned. The ID is not sent to the model.
    
    Redis stores at most eight completed turns, with a 30-minute idle expiry
    refreshed after a successful turn. The active conversation retains the existing
    128 KiB message limit; old turns are removed as complete exchanges when room
    is needed. This is short-term context, not durable chat history. Stored data
    is bound to the authenticated user, membership, workspace, and role. An ID
    cannot carry admin history into a member request or cross workspace/user
    boundaries. Every request still traverses the existing auth/membership chain.
    
    The loop rebuilds the system instruction and reads current context on every
    turn. It uses old exchanges to interpret clarifications and instructs the
    model to refresh workspace facts through tools. Historical tool messages keep
    their untrusted-data envelopes; their call IDs are remapped to avoid collisions
    with new calls. Strict stored-message validation rejects system/developer
    messages, broken tool exchanges, oversized records, and unsupported tools.
    Conversation history never authorizes a write or approves a proposal.
    
    Atomic Redis scripts acquire a turn lease and save a completed transcript only
    while that lease still belongs to the request. Concurrent requests receive
    409 `AGENT_CONVERSATION_BUSY` before a model call. The lease expires after ten
    minutes; a late request cannot overwrite or release a newer request's lease.
    A lost lease or transcript expiry during a turn returns 409
    `AGENT_CONVERSATION_CONFLICT`. Failed turns retain the previous transcript;
    failed first turns discard their unpublished record when cleanup is available.
    
    Unknown, expired, or differently scoped IDs return the same 404
    `AGENT_CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND`. Redis failure or corrupt history returns 503
    `AGENT_CONVERSATION_UNAVAILABLE`; history is never silently replaced with an
    empty conversation. Redis commands have a one-second deadline. An already
    submitted command may complete after that deadline; leases and records still
    expire. A persistence failure can occur after provider usage has been charged.
    Stateless requests remain available under the existing Redis-outage behavior.
    
    Unit tests cover real Lua scripts with ioredis-mock, storage failures, scope
    changes, lease races, history limits, clarification turns, and the real HTTP
    composition with mocked transports. Actual Redis expiry/atomicity and live
    model follow-up, prompt-injection, and numerical-fidelity evaluations remain
    integration/evaluation work.
    
    ## Internal read loop
    
    `runReadTurn({ data: { message }, context, provider })` in
    `services/read-loop.service.js` runs one fresh read-only turn. Server code
    supplies the authenticated context and the provider. Client data accepts only
    a text message; conversation history, roles, tool results, and workspace IDs
    are rejected. Each invocation starts with `get_my_context` and keeps its
    messages and authenticated identity local to that invocation.
    
    `runReadTurnWithHistory` is the internal stateful variant. It accepts validated
    server-owned history separately from client `data` and returns `{ reply,
    history }` to the conversation service for storage. Neither interface accepts
    history in the client's message object. Current tool/model-call limits apply
    per turn, excluding the exchanges restored from previous turns.
    
    The injected provider implements:
    
    ```js
    provider.chat({ messages, tools, trace })
    // -> { text: string | null, toolCalls: [{ id, name, arguments: string }], usage? }
    // usage: { promptTokens, completionTokens, totalTokens } | null
    ```
    
    Messages use chat-completion roles and correlated `tool_call_id` values.
    Tool definitions contain `name`, `description`, and the Zod `parameterSchema`;
    the provider adapter owns converting schemas to its wire format. Only the
    caller's permitted Tier 0/1 definitions are supplied. Every execution still
    passes through `executeReadTool` and the handler's permission checks.
    
    Tool messages wrap results in `{ kind: 'untrusted_tool_result', data }`, and
    the fixed system instruction treats their contents as data and forbids
    arithmetic. This preserves the instruction/data boundary; live-model prompt
    injection and numerical-fidelity evaluations are still required.
    
    The loop permits at most 6 model calls and 12 tool calls (including context),
    8,000 input characters, 16,000 reply characters, 64 KiB per tool result, and
    128 KiB of conversation messages. It rejects unavailable tools, reused call
    IDs, malformed responses/arguments, and oversized results. Errors terminate
    the turn; transport and unexpected service details are not returned to callers.
    Success returns `{ text, modelCalls, toolCalls }`. Turn and tool traces share
    a server-generated `turnId`; rejected batches identify their requested tools.
    Provider calls receive a separate server-owned `trace` with the HTTP request
    ID (when available), turn ID, workspace/caller IDs, and model-call index. The
    Groq adapter uses this only for local logs; it is not sent to the model.
    
    ## Token accounting and budget scope
    
    The adapter normalizes provider-reported prompt, completion, and total token
    counts. Counts must be nonnegative safe integers, and the total must equal
    prompt plus completion tokens. Unknown provider metadata is discarded.
    Missing usage remains `null`, not a claim of zero consumption.
    
    Usage is parsed before completion validation. A truncated or rejected
    completion can therefore retain valid usage on its canonical error's internal
    `usage` property. Normalization preserves only validated counts; that property
    is separate from client-facing error details and is not serialized into HTTP
    errors. Unreadable bodies, timeouts without usage, and invalid usage remain
    unreported. Successful HTTP responses also keep their existing shape.
    
    Each turn's success or failure trace contains a `usage` summary:
    `knownPromptTokens`, `knownCompletionTokens`, `knownTotalTokens`,
    `reportedModelCalls`, `unreportedModelCalls`, and `complete`. Totals include
    reported usage from failed completions and calls followed by tool failures.
    `complete` describes accounting coverage, not whether the turn succeeded.
    When usage is incomplete, the known totals are only a partial count. The loop
    rejects aggregate totals that cannot be represented safely instead of rounding.
    
    The chat service applies **one shared allowance per workspace**, defaulting to
    **100,000 input plus output tokens per UTC day**. Server configuration:
    
    | Setting | Default | Range |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `AGENT_WORKSPACE_TOKEN_LIMIT` | `100000` | 1–1,000,000,000 tokens |
    | `AGENT_BUDGET_PERIOD` | `day` | `day` or `month` (UTC calendar windows) |
    | `AGENT_BUDGET_TIMEOUT_MS` | `3000` | 1–10,000 milliseconds |
    
    Before every Groq call, the adapter reserves the UTF-8 byte size of the entire
    serialized request plus its maximum completion tokens. This conservative
    estimate includes messages and tool definitions; it is not an exact tokenizer
    or dollar billing cap. Actual provider usage replaces the reservation after
    successful or rejected completions. Missing usage keeps the reservation.
    Redis outages allow calls without budget accounting. Traces retain reported
    usage, but there is no automatic replay of missed accounting after recovery.
    Budget denials occur before transport and do not count as model calls.
    
    ### Internal workspace budget service
    
    `createWorkspaceBudget({ context, limit, period, timeoutMs? })` in
    `services/budget.service.js` provides an internal reservation/reconciliation
    primitive used by the chat service. `period` supports `day` or `month` with UTC
    calendar resets; `limit` is a positive token count. Identity comes from
    authenticated server context. Budget settings cannot come from chat input.
    
    `reserve({ tokens })` atomically reserves against one Redis hash per workspace
    and window and returns an immutable reservation. `settle({ reservation, usage })`
    replaces that reservation with validated provider token usage exactly once.
    Usage above the reservation is fully charged; unknown usage retains the
    reservation. Later known usage can reconcile a held reservation. Pending and
    settled records expire one hour after the window resets, allowing in-flight
    calls to settle against their original window. The active window uses the
    lowest configured allowance seen during rolling deployments; increases take
    effect in the next window.
    
    Redis outages **do not block the caller**: missing/not-ready clients, command
    errors, and the bounded command timeout (default 3 seconds) return `null` from
    `reserve`. Passing that null reservation to `settle` returns
    `{ state: 'unavailable' }`; a settlement outage returns the same state. These
    outcomes are logged without upstream error details. There is no local quota
    balance, no automatic retry, and no claim that skipped calls were charged.
    A command already sent to Redis may finish after the deadline, leaving a
    conservative reservation. A settlement outage retains any stored reservation.
    
    A confirmed exhausted allowance returns `AGENT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` (429) with an
    internal reset timestamp, converted to `Retry-After` by the controller; a
    reservation above the entire allowance returns
    `AGENT_BUDGET_REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` (422). Invalid configuration or corrupt/missing
    accounting state returns a typed 503 rather than resetting balances. Once the
    provider has run, settlement failures are logged without discarding its reply
    or masking its original error. Stored reservations remain charged.
    
    `tests/unit/agent/budget.test.js` exercises the Lua scripts using ioredis-mock,
    including workspace isolation, duplicate settlement, unknown usage, UTC
    windows, and unavailable Redis. Real Redis atomicity, expiry, and network
    failure behavior still need integration coverage. `chat-outage.test.js` runs
    real request middleware with mocked stalled/reconnecting Redis transports,
    checking successful chat and continued membership denial during outages.
    
    Streaming remains a subsequent increment.
    
    ## Groq adapter
    
    `providers/groq.provider.js` exports `createGroqProvider()`, which implements
    the loop's provider interface using Node's built-in `fetch`:
    
    ```js
    const { createGroqProvider } = require('./providers/groq.provider');
    const { runReadTurn } = require('./services/read-loop.service');
    const provider = createGroqProvider();
    const reply = await runReadTurn({ data: { message }, context, provider });
    ```
    
    This low-level example omits budgeting. Production HTTP chat uses
    `runChatTurn`, which supplies the authenticated workspace budget to the adapter.
    
    Set `GROQ_API_KEY` and `GROQ_MODEL` on the server; both are required. Choose a
    standard model that supports function calling. Compound model IDs are rejected
    because those systems can execute provider-hosted tools outside Kith. Only
    function definitions already selected by the loop are sent to Groq, and
    responses that contain provider-executed or undeclared tools are rejected.
    
    The adapter converts Zod input schemas using `zod-to-json-schema`. This gives
    the model structural constraints; the registry remains responsible for full
    Zod validation, including refinements and transformations. Handler functions,
    server context objects, and credentials are not serialized into tool definitions.
    
    `GROQ_TIMEOUT_MS` defaults to 20000 (maximum 60000) and covers both the request
    and response-body read. `GROQ_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS` defaults to 1024 (maximum
    4096). Requests and streamed response bodies are capped at 256 KiB. The
    endpoint is fixed to Groq's HTTPS chat-completions API, redirects are rejected,
    and requests are non-streaming with one completion and no automatic retries.
    
    Successful responses normalize to `{ text, toolCalls, usage }`.
    Truncated, malformed, or inconsistent completions terminate the turn. Timeout
    and rate-limit codes survive the loop boundary, but upstream messages, bodies,
    reasoning fields, and credentials are not exposed to callers or logs. Provider
    token usage, model, HTTP status, latency, and server trace IDs are logged.
    
    Unit tests use synthetic Groq responses, Web Streams, and the real read loop.
    They do not make live model calls or verify a deployed model's behavior.
    Reference: [Groq chat API](https://console.groq.com/docs/api-reference#chat-create)
    and [tool use](https://console.groq.com/docs/tool-use).
    
    ## Database and verification
    
    The source of truth is `migrations/001_schema.sql`: it adds `pg_trgm`, two GIN
    indexes, and `search_members_ranked` / `search_containers_ranked`. Existing
    `pg_trgm` installations in either `public` or `extensions` are supported.
    The RPCs receive the escaped pattern from the shared `containsPattern` helper.
    
    For an existing database, apply only these additions, with function creation
    and permission changes in the same transaction; do not replay the consolidated
    schema against existing tables. RPC execution is revoked from PUBLIC and
    Supabase browser roles and granted to `service_role` when present. Schema edits
    in the repository do not update a running database or its PostgREST schema cache.
    Reload that cache after applying the additions and before exercising the tools.
    
    Run `npm run test:unit -- --runInBand` from `backend`. Real trigram ranking,
    workspace filtering, wildcard handling, and RPC permissions are covered by
    `tests/integration/database/ranked-search.test.js`. Run that suite with

     *

     * schema.txt's FK constraints on containers/groups/milestones/
     * invite_links/workspace_members, all of which cascade from
     * workspace_id) — deleting the workspace row itself is usually

     * first to avoid FK violations on the workspace delete.

    // are protected by BEFORE DELETE triggers, so PostgREST deletes of them
    // always fail with P0001 and then the workspace delete fails its FK
    // (23503), leaving every seeded workspace behind. Test-only escape hatch:
    // a direct connection with session_replication_role = replica, which
    // skips triggers (and FK enforcement) for that one transaction. The
    // triggers stay in force for the app and for every other test path.
    // Only the protected/non-cascading tables are removed this way; the
    // workspace itself is then deleted normally so ON DELETE CASCADE runs.
    let _pgPool = null;
    function getPgPool() {
      if (!_pgPool) {
        const { Pool } = require('pg');
        _pgPool = new Pool({
          connectionString: process.env.TEST_DATABASE_URL
            || 'postgres://postgres:test@localhost:54322/kith_test', // docker-compose.test.yml / CI
          max: 2,
          idleTimeoutMillis: 1000,
          allowExitOnIdle: true,
        });
      }
      return _pgPool;
    }
    
    // Tables with no workspace_id column of their own, keyed through a parent
    // that has one. Must be removed BEFORE the parent rows (the subqueries
    // need the parents to still exist). With FK enforcement off in replica
    // mode, order only matters for these subqueries.
    const CHILD_TABLE_PURGES = [
      ['cycle_carry_forwards',    'container_id', 'containers'],
      ['contributor_targets',     'container_id', 'containers'],
      ['container_cycles',        'container_id', 'containers'],
      ['container_participants',  'container_id', 'containers'],
      ['container_tasks',         'container_id', 'containers'],
      ['pool_cycle_overrides',    'container_id', 'containers'],
      ['group_members',           'group_id',     'groups'],
      ['member_profile_audit',    'workspace_member_id', 'workspace_members'],
      ['notification_deliveries', 'notification_id', 'notifications'],
    ];
    
    async function purgeProtectedRows(workspaceId) {
      const client = await getPgPool().connect();
      try {
        await client.query('BEGIN');
        // Skips triggers AND FK enforcement/cascades for this transaction only,
        // so the whole workspace is removed explicitly here instead of relying
        // on ON DELETE CASCADE ordering (which also trips on non-cascading
        // FKs into workspace_members, e.g. container_participants).
        await client.query("SET LOCAL session_replication_role = 'replica'");
    
        for (const [table, col, parent] of CHILD_TABLE_PURGES) {
          await client.query(
            `DELETE FROM public.${table} WHERE ${col} IN (SELECT id FROM public.${parent} WHERE workspace_id = $1)`,
            [workspaceId]
          );
        }
    
        const { rows } = await client.query(
          `SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.columns
            WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND column_name = 'workspace_id'
              AND table_name <> 'workspaces'
              AND table_name IN (SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables
                                  WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_type = 'BASE TABLE')`
        );
        for (const { table_name } of rows) {
          await client.query(`DELETE FROM public."${table_name}" WHERE workspace_id = $1`, [workspaceId]);
        }
    
        await client.query('DELETE FROM public.workspaces WHERE id = $1', [workspaceId]);
        await client.query('COMMIT');
        return true;
      } catch (err) {
        await client.query('ROLLBACK').catch(() => {});
        if (!purgeProtectedRows.warned) {
          purgeProtectedRows.warned = true;
          console.warn(`cleanupWorkspace: direct purge unavailable (${err.message}); set TEST_DATABASE_URL. Falling back to PostgREST deletes.`);
        }
        return false;
      } finally {
        client.release();
      }
    }
    
    async function cleanupWorkspace(supabaseAdmin, workspaceId) {
      const purged = await purgeProtectedRows(workspaceId);
    
      if (!purged) {
        // Fallback (no direct DB access): best effort via PostgREST.
        const { error: e1 } = await supabaseAdmin.from('ledger_entries').delete().eq('workspace_id', workspaceId);
        if (e1) console.error('cleanupWorkspace: ledger_entries error:', e1);
        const { error: e2 } = await supabaseAdmin.from('disputes').delete().eq('workspace_id', workspaceId);
        if (e2) console.error('cleanupWorkspace: disputes error:', e2);
        const { error: e4 } = await supabaseAdmin.from('audit_log').delete().eq('workspace_id', workspaceId);
        if (e4) console.error('cleanupWorkspace: audit_log error:', e4);
      }
    
      const { error: e3 } = await supabaseAdmin.from('notifications').delete().eq('workspace_id', workspaceId);
      if (e3) console.error('cleanupWorkspace: notifications error:', e3);
    
      const { error: e5 } = await supabaseAdmin.from('workspace_settings').delete().eq('workspace_id', workspaceId);
      if (e5) console.error('cleanupWorkspace: workspace_settings error:', e5);
    
      const { error: e6 } = await supabaseAdmin.from('workspaces').delete().eq('id', workspaceId);
      if (e6) console.error('cleanupWorkspace: workspaces error:', e6);
    }
    
    module.exports = {
      seedWorkspaceWithAdmin,
      seedAdditionalMember,
      seedContainerWithParticipants,
      seedLedgerEntry,
      seedGroupWithMembers,
      seedMilestone,
      seedInviteLink,
      cleanupWorkspace,
    };

    CREATE INDEX idx_ledger_cycle ON public.ledger_entries USING btree (cycle_id) WHERE (cycle_id IS NOT NULL);
    
    CREATE INDEX idx_ledger_recorded_at ON public.ledger_entries USING btree (recorded_at DESC);

    -- Lock confirmed/disputed/resolved ledger entries at the DB level.
    -- ledger.service.js already refuses to touch an entry once it leaves
    -- 'pending'/'proof_uploaded' (updateEntry/deleteEntry) — this adds the
    -- same rule as a trigger, so it holds even for anything with the
    -- service-role key, not just requests that go through the app layer.
    CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.enforce_ledger_entry_immutability()
    RETURNS trigger
    LANGUAGE plpgsql
    AS $$
    BEGIN
      IF OLD.status NOT IN ('confirmed', 'disputed', 'resolved') THEN
        RETURN NEW; -- pending / proof_uploaded entries remain freely editable
      END IF;
    
      -- Once locked, `status` may only move through a whitelisted
      -- transition, matching what raise_dispute_atomic and
      -- resolve_dispute_atomic actually do. A pending -> disputed move
      -- never reaches this branch: it's covered by the early RETURN NEW
      -- above, since OLD.status = 'pending' isn't in the locked list.
      -- Extend this list if a future 'reversed' flow is built.
      IF NEW.status IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.status THEN
        IF NOT (
          (OLD.status = 'confirmed' AND NEW.status = 'disputed') OR
          (OLD.status = 'disputed'  AND NEW.status = 'resolved')
        ) THEN
          RAISE EXCEPTION 'ledger_entries: % -> % is not an allowed status transition for entry % (currently %)',
            OLD.status, NEW.status, OLD.id, OLD.status;
        END IF;
      END IF;
    
      -- Every other column is frozen once confirmed. `proofs` is excluded:
      -- ledger.service.js confirmProof/deleteProof both write to `proofs`
      -- on a possibly-locked entry (deleteProof lets an admin remove a
      -- proof from a confirmed entry). `status` is handled above.
      IF (to_jsonb(NEW) - 'status' - 'proofs') IS DISTINCT FROM (to_jsonb(OLD) - 'status' - 'proofs') THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'ledger_entries: entry % is locked (status=%) — only its status (via an allowed transition) and proofs may change. Use a correction (corrects_entry_id) to adjust a confirmed entry instead.',
          OLD.id, OLD.status;
      END IF;
    
      RETURN NEW;
    END;
    $$;
    
    CREATE TRIGGER trg_ledger_entries_lock_confirmed BEFORE UPDATE ON public.ledger_entries FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.enforce_ledger_entry_immutability();
    
    CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.prevent_locked_ledger_entry_delete()
    RETURNS trigger
    LANGUAGE plpgsql
    AS $$
    BEGIN
      IF OLD.status IN ('confirmed', 'disputed', 'resolved') THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'ledger_entries: entry % cannot be deleted once confirmed (status=%). Use a correction instead.',
          OLD.id, OLD.status;
      END IF;
      RETURN OLD;
    END;
    $$;
    
    CREATE TRIGGER trg_ledger_entries_prevent_locked_delete BEFORE DELETE ON public.ledger_entries FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.prevent_locked_ledger_entry_delete();

    CREATE FUNCTION public.search_tasks_ranked(
        p_workspace_id uuid, p_caller_id uuid, p_is_admin boolean,
        p_query text, p_pattern text, p_limit integer DEFAULT 11, p_container_id uuid DEFAULT NULL
    ) RETURNS TABLE (id uuid, container_id uuid, title text, assigned_to uuid, status text, due_date date, match_type text, score real)
        LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY INVOKER
        SET search_path TO pg_catalog, public, extensions, pg_temp
        SET pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold TO '0.3'
        AS $$
        WITH actor AS (
            SELECT m.id, (coalesce(p_is_admin, false) AND m.role = 'admin') AS is_admin
            FROM public.workspace_members m
            JOIN public.workspaces w ON w.id = m.workspace_id AND w.deleted_at IS NULL
            WHERE m.id = p_caller_id AND m.workspace_id = p_workspace_id
              AND m.is_active = true AND m.deleted_at IS NULL AND m.role IN ('member', 'admin')
        ), matches AS (
            SELECT t.id, t.container_id, t.title, t.assigned_to, t.status, t.due_date,
                CASE WHEN lower(t.title) = lower(p_query) THEN 'exact'
                     WHEN t.title ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\' THEN 'substring'
                     ELSE 'fuzzy' END AS match_type,
                greatest(similarity(p_query, t.title), word_similarity(p_query, t.title)) AS score
            FROM public.container_tasks t
            JOIN public.containers c ON c.id = t.container_id
            CROSS JOIN actor a
            WHERE c.workspace_id = p_workspace_id AND c.deleted_at IS NULL AND t.deleted_at IS NULL
              AND (a.is_admin OR t.assigned_to = a.id)
              AND (p_container_id IS NULL OR t.container_id = p_container_id)
              AND char_length(p_query) BETWEEN 2 AND 200
              AND (t.title ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\'
                   OR (char_length(p_query) >= 3 AND t.title %> p_query))
        )
        SELECT m.id, m.container_id, m.title, m.assigned_to, m.status, m.due_date, m.match_type, m.score
        FROM matches m
        ORDER BY CASE m.match_type WHEN 'exact' THEN 0 WHEN 'substring' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END,
                 m.score DESC, lower(m.title) COLLATE "C", m.id
        LIMIT least(21, greatest(2, coalesce(p_limit, 11)));
    $$;
