                greatest(similarity(p_query, d.reason), word_similarity(p_query, d.reason),
                         similarity(p_query, raiser.display_name), word_similarity(p_query, raiser.display_name),
                         similarity(p_query, e.note), word_similarity(p_query, e.note), 0::real) AS score
            FROM public.disputes d
            LEFT JOIN public.workspace_members raiser
              ON raiser.id = d.raised_by AND raiser.workspace_id = p_workspace_id
            LEFT JOIN public.ledger_entries e
              ON e.id = d.ledger_entry_id AND e.workspace_id = p_workspace_id
            CROSS JOIN actor a
            WHERE d.workspace_id = p_workspace_id AND (a.is_admin OR d.raised_by = a.id)
              AND char_length(p_query) BETWEEN 2 AND 200
              AND (d.reason ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\' OR raiser.display_name ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\'
                   OR e.note ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\'
                   OR (char_length(p_query) >= 3 AND (d.reason %> p_query OR raiser.display_name %> p_query OR e.note %> p_query)))
        )
        SELECT m.id, m.ledger_entry_id, m.raised_by, m.raised_by_name, m.reason, m.status, m.raised_at, m.match_type, m.score
        FROM matches m
        ORDER BY CASE m.match_type WHEN 'exact' THEN 0 WHEN 'substring' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END,
                 m.score DESC, lower(m.reason) COLLATE "C", m.id
        LIMIT least(21, greatest(2, coalesce(p_limit, 11)));
    $$;
    
    CREATE FUNCTION public.search_groups_ranked(
        p_workspace_id uuid, p_query text, p_pattern text, p_limit integer DEFAULT 11
    ) RETURNS TABLE (id uuid, name text, description text, created_at timestamp with time zone, match_type text, score real)
        LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY INVOKER
        SET search_path TO pg_catalog, public, extensions, pg_temp
        SET pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold TO '0.3'
        AS $$
        WITH matches AS (
            SELECT g.id, g.name, g.description, g.created_at,
                CASE WHEN lower(g.name) = lower(p_query) THEN 'exact'
                     WHEN g.name ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\' THEN 'substring'
                     ELSE 'fuzzy' END AS match_type,
                greatest(similarity(p_query, g.name), word_similarity(p_query, g.name)) AS score
            FROM public.groups g
            WHERE g.workspace_id = p_workspace_id AND char_length(p_query) BETWEEN 2 AND 200
              AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.workspaces w WHERE w.id = p_workspace_id AND w.deleted_at IS NULL)
              AND (g.name ILIKE p_pattern ESCAPE E'\\' OR (char_length(p_query) >= 3 AND g.name %> p_query))
        )
        SELECT m.id, m.name, m.description, m.created_at, m.match_type, m.score
        FROM matches m
        ORDER BY CASE m.match_type WHEN 'exact' THEN 0 WHEN 'substring' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END,
                 m.score DESC, lower(m.name) COLLATE "C", m.id
        LIMIT least(21, greatest(2, coalesce(p_limit, 11)));
    $$;
    
    REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION
        public.search_tasks_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer, uuid),
        public.search_ledger_entries_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer, uuid),
        public.search_disputes_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer),
        public.search_groups_ranked(uuid, text, text, integer) FROM PUBLIC;
    
    DO $$
    DECLARE browser_role text;
    BEGIN
        FOR browser_role IN SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname IN ('anon', 'authenticated') LOOP
            EXECUTE format('REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.search_tasks_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer, uuid), public.search_ledger_entries_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer, uuid), public.search_disputes_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer), public.search_groups_ranked(uuid, text, text, integer) FROM %I', browser_role);
        END LOOP;
        IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'service_role') THEN
            GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA extensions TO service_role;
            GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION
                public.search_tasks_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer, uuid),
                public.search_ledger_entries_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer, uuid),
                public.search_disputes_ranked(uuid, uuid, boolean, text, text, integer),
                public.search_groups_ranked(uuid, text, text, integer) TO service_role;
        END IF;
    END;
    $$;

    // src/services/search.service.js
    //
    // Query-building/escaping/shaping logic for cross-entity search. The
    // controller is a thin HTTP adapter around this.
    
    const { supabaseAdmin } = require('../config/supabase');
    const { containsPattern } = require('../utils/ilike');
    const { AppError, ValidationError } = require('../utils/errors');
    const { entitySearchRequestSchema, callerEntitySearchRequestSchema, callerContainerSearchRequestSchema } = require('../validators/search.validator');
    const logger = require('../utils/logger');
    
    /**
     * Cross-entity search across active members (by display_name) and
     * containers (by name) in parallel. Results are typed so the client can
     * render them differently. Scoped to the current workspace.
     *
     * ILIKE wildcard escaping is shared via utils/ilike.js.
     *
     * @returns {Promise<{results: Array, query: string}>}
     */
    async function searchWorkspace({ workspaceId, query, limit = 10 }) {
      const trimmedQuery = (query || '').trim();
      const safeLimit    = Math.min(20, parseInt(limit) || 10);
    
      if (!trimmedQuery || trimmedQuery.length < 2) {
        return { results: [], query: trimmedQuery };
      }
    
      const pattern = containsPattern(trimmedQuery);
    
      const [{ data: members }, { data: containers }] = await Promise.all([
        supabaseAdmin
          .from('workspace_members')
          .select('id, display_name, role, is_proxy')
          .eq('workspace_id', workspaceId)
          .eq('is_active', true)
          .is('deleted_at', null)
          .ilike('display_name', pattern)
          .limit(safeLimit),
    
        supabaseAdmin
          .from('containers')
          .select('id, name, container_type, status')
          .eq('workspace_id', workspaceId)
          .is('deleted_at', null)
          .ilike('name', pattern)
          .limit(safeLimit),
      ]);
    
      const results = [
        ...(members    || []).map((m) => ({ type: 'member',    id: m.id, display_name: m.display_name, role: m.role, is_proxy: m.is_proxy })),
        ...(containers || []).map((c) => ({ type: 'container', id: c.id, name: c.name, container_type: c.container_type, status: c.status })),
      ];
    
      return { results, query: trimmedQuery };
    }
    
    /**
     * Shared adapter for the ranked entity RPCs. All results are
     * candidates: single_match still needs user confirmation before a write.
     * Scores are database similarities, not probabilities or proof of identity.
     */
    async function findCandidates(params, rpcName, shapeCandidate, { requestSchema = entitySearchRequestSchema, rpcScope = () => ({}) } = {}) {
      const parsed = requestSchema.safeParse(params);
      if (!parsed.success) {
        throw new ValidationError('Invalid entity search', null, parsed.error.issues);
      }
      const { workspaceId, query, limit } = parsed.data;
    
      let rows;
      try {
        const { data, error } = await supabaseAdmin.rpc(rpcName, {
          p_workspace_id: workspaceId,
          p_query: query,
          p_pattern: containsPattern(query),
          p_limit: limit + 1,
          ...rpcScope(parsed.data),
        });
        if (error || !Array.isArray(data) || data.some((row) => !row || typeof row !== 'object' || Array.isArray(row))) {
          logger.error('Ranked entity search failed', { workspaceId, rpcName, error: error?.message || 'Invalid RPC result' });
          throw new AppError('Entity search is unavailable. Please try again.', 503, 'SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE');
        }
        rows = data;
      } catch (err) {
        if (err instanceof AppError) throw err;
        logger.error('Ranked entity search failed', { workspaceId, rpcName, error: err.message });
        throw new AppError('Entity search is unavailable. Please try again.', 503, 'SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE');
      }
    
      // Determine ambiguity before truncation. Never select the highest-scoring
      // candidate on behalf of the caller, even if it is an exact match.
      return {
        query,
        status: rows.length === 0 ? 'not_found' : rows.length === 1 ? 'single_match' : 'ambiguous',
        candidates: rows.slice(0, limit).map(shapeCandidate),
        has_more: rows.length > limit,
      };
    }
    
    async function findMembers(params) {
      return findCandidates(params, 'search_members_ranked', (row) => ({
        id: row.id, display_name: row.display_name, role: row.role, is_proxy: row.is_proxy,
        match_type: row.match_type, score: row.score,
      }));
    }
    
    async function findContainers(params) {
      return findCandidates(params, 'search_containers_ranked', (row) => ({
        id: row.id, name: row.name, container_type: row.container_type, status: row.status,
        match_type: row.match_type, score: row.score,
      }));
    }
    
    const callerRpcScope = ({ callerId, isAdmin }) => ({ p_caller_id: callerId, p_is_admin: isAdmin });
    const containerCallerRpcScope = (params) => ({ ...callerRpcScope(params), p_container_id: params.containerId ?? null });
    
    async function findTasks(params) {
      return findCandidates(params, 'search_tasks_ranked', (row) => ({
        id: row.id, container_id: row.container_id, title: row.title, assigned_to: row.assigned_to,
        status: row.status, due_date: row.due_date, match_type: row.match_type, score: row.score,
      }), { requestSchema: callerContainerSearchRequestSchema, rpcScope: containerCallerRpcScope });
    }
    
    async function findLedgerEntries(params) {
      return findCandidates(params, 'search_ledger_entries_ranked', (row) => ({
        id: row.id, container_id: row.container_id, contributor_id: row.contributor_id, contributor_name: row.contributor_name,
        note: row.note, original_amount: row.original_amount, original_currency: row.original_currency,
        entry_type: row.entry_type, status: row.status, recorded_at: row.recorded_at, match_type: row.match_type, score: row.score,
      }), { requestSchema: callerContainerSearchRequestSchema, rpcScope: containerCallerRpcScope });
    }
    
    async function findDisputes(params) {
      return findCandidates(params, 'search_disputes_ranked', (row) => ({
        id: row.id, ledger_entry_id: row.ledger_entry_id, raised_by: row.raised_by, raised_by_name: row.raised_by_name,
        reason: row.reason, status: row.status, raised_at: row.raised_at, match_type: row.match_type, score: row.score,
      }), { requestSchema: callerEntitySearchRequestSchema, rpcScope: callerRpcScope });
    }
    
    async function findGroups(params) {
      return findCandidates(params, 'search_groups_ranked', (row) => ({
        id: row.id, name: row.name, description: row.description, created_at: row.created_at, match_type: row.match_type, score: row.score,
      }));
    }
    
    module.exports = { searchWorkspace, findMembers, findContainers, findTasks, findLedgerEntries, findDisputes, findGroups };
    
    const { z } = require('zod');
    
    // At least two choices can be displayed when the query is ambiguous.
    const entitySearchSchema = z.object({
      query: z.string().trim().min(2).max(200),
      limit: z.number().int().min(2).max(20).optional().default(10),
    }).strict();
    
    const entitySearchRequestSchema = entitySearchSchema.extend({
      workspaceId: z.string().uuid(),
    });
    
    const containerEntitySearchSchema = entitySearchSchema.extend({ container_id: z.string().uuid().optional() });
    const callerEntitySearchRequestSchema = entitySearchRequestSchema.extend({
      callerId: z.string().uuid(), isAdmin: z.boolean(),
    });
    const callerContainerSearchRequestSchema = callerEntitySearchRequestSchema.extend({ containerId: z.string().uuid().optional() });
    
    module.exports = {
      entitySearchSchema, entitySearchRequestSchema, containerEntitySearchSchema,
      callerEntitySearchRequestSchema, callerContainerSearchRequestSchema,
    };

    // tests/setup.unit.js
    //
    // Runs via Jest's `setupFilesAfterEnv` for the "unit" project — AFTER the
    // test framework itself is initialised but BEFORE any test file's own
    // top-level code executes. This ordering matters: it's what lets us set
    // process.env here and have it already be in place by the time a test
    // file's `require('../../src/services/whatever.service')` transitively
    // pulls in config/supabase.js, which reads these vars at module-load
    // time and calls process.exit(1) if they're missing (see
    // config/supabase.js's top-level guard). A beforeAll() inside an
    // individual test file would run too late for that.
    //
    // Unit tests NEVER talk to real Postgres/Redis — every DB/Redis call is
    // mocked at the module level (see tests/mocks/*). These env vars exist
    // purely so config/supabase.js's startup guard and any code that reads
    // process.env.FRONTEND_URL / etc. don't crash before the mocks take
    // over.
    
    process.env.NODE_ENV = 'test';
    
    process.env.SUPABASE_URL = 'https://test.supabase.local';
    process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY = 'test-service-role-key';
    process.env.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY = 'test-anon-key';
    
    process.env.REDIS_URL = 'redis://localhost:6379/1';
    
    process.env.FRONTEND_URL = 'https://app.test.local';
    process.env.API_BASE_URL = 'http://localhost:3000';
    
    process.env.STORAGE_BUCKET_NAME = 'kith-files-test';
    
    process.env.RESEND_API_KEY = '';        // intentionally unset-like — exercises the "not configured" branches
    process.env.FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT = ''; // same
    
    process.env.ALLOWED_DEEPLINK_SCHEMES = 'kithapp://';
    
    process.env.IDEMPOTENCY_ENABLED = 'true';
    process.env.FILE_VERIFICATION_ENABLED = 'true';
    
    process.env.LOG_LEVEL = 'silent'; // keep test output clean; winston still initialises fine with this
    
    // Silence winston's console transport noise in unit test output while
    // still letting logger.* calls execute (so code paths that pass a
    // logger call aren't accidentally skipped/erroring).
    jest.mock('../src/utils/logger', () => ({
      info:  jest.fn(),
      warn:  jest.fn(),
      error: jest.fn(),
      debug: jest.fn(),
    }));
    
    // Global test lifecycle hygiene
    afterEach(() => {
      jest.clearAllMocks();
    });
    
    // tests/setup.integration.js
    //
    // Runs via Jest's `setupFilesAfterEnv` for the "integration" project.
    // Integration tests hit REAL Postgres (docker-compose.test.yml's
    // postgres-test service) and REAL Redis (redis-test), but mock external
    // SaaS (Firebase/Resend) always — see tests/mocks/firebase.mock.js and
    // tests/mocks/resend.mock.js, and Doc 3 Section 1's "mock external SaaS
    // always" rule referenced in tests/mocks/README.md.
    //
    // process.env.NODE_ENV stays 'test' here (unlike setup.ratelimit.js)
    // specifically so rateLimiter.js's `skip: (req) => process.env.NODE_ENV
    // === 'test'` bypasses rate limiting for every OTHER integration suite —
    // only tests/integration/redis/rate-limiting.test.js needs limiters to
    // actually engage, and that suite runs under the separate "rate-limit"
    // Jest project (setup.ratelimit.js) specifically to get a different
    // NODE_ENV before its own app.js import happens.
    
    const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken');
    
    process.env.NODE_ENV = 'test';
    
    // FIX (see docker-compose.test.yml's header comment): SUPABASE_URL must
    // point at PostgREST (the REST API layer supabase-js actually talks to),
    // not at Postgres's own wire-protocol port. Overridable via
    // TEST_SUPABASE_URL for CI or alternate local setups.
    process.env.SUPABASE_URL ='http://localhost:3001';
    
    // FIX: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY / SUPABASE_ANON_KEY must be real signed
    // JWTs, not plain placeholder strings — PostgREST decodes the bearer
    // token as a JWT (header.payload.signature) to determine which Postgres
    // role to SET ROLE as via the `role` claim. A non-JWT string fails with
    // JWSError (CompactDecodeError: Expected 3 parts; got 1) on every query.
    // Signed with the same secret docker-compose.test.yml's PGRST_JWT_SECRET
    // uses (both read from TEST_JWT_SECRET so they can't drift apart).
    // role: 'postgres' matches PGRST_DB_ANON_ROLE in docker-compose.test.yml;
    // role: 'anon' is the conventional PostgREST anon-client role.
    const JWT_SECRET = process.env.TEST_JWT_SECRET || 'test-jwt-secret-at-least-32-characters-long';
    process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY = process.env.TEST_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY || jwt.sign({ role: 'postgres' }, JWT_SECRET);
    process.env.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY = process.env.TEST_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY || jwt.sign({ role: 'anon' }, JWT_SECRET);
    
    // Dedicated Redis DB index (1) so this never collides with a developer's
    // local dev-server Redis (DB 0) if both happen to be running against the
    // same Redis host/port during local test runs.
    process.env.REDIS_URL = 'redis://localhost:63790/1';
    
    process.env.FRONTEND_URL = 'https://app.test.local';
    process.env.API_BASE_URL = 'http://localhost:3000';
    process.env.STORAGE_BUCKET_NAME = 'kith-files-test';
    process.env.ALLOWED_DEEPLINK_SCHEMES = 'kithapp://';
    process.env.IDEMPOTENCY_ENABLED = 'true';
    process.env.FILE_VERIFICATION_ENABLED = 'false'; // integration tests don't upload real bytes to real storage by default
    process.env.LOG_LEVEL = 'silent';
    process.env.JWT_SECRET = 'test-secret';
    
    // External SaaS mocks — ALWAYS mocked, even in integration tests, per
    // Doc 3 Section 1. Real Postgres/Redis, fake Firebase/Resend.
    jest.mock('../src/config/firebase', () => require('./mocks/firebase.mock'));
    jest.mock('../src/config/resend',   () => require('./mocks/resend.mock'));
    jest.setTimeout(30000);
    const { getRedis } = require('../src/config/redis');
    
    // Doc 4 Section 2.4: Redis is FLUSHDB'd between test FILES (not
    // individual tests) — every test within a file that touches
    // Redis-cached data must use a freshly-generated workspace/user ID per
    // test (via factory counters) rather than a shared constant ID, to avoid
    // one test's cached state leaking into the next test in the SAME file.
    // See tests/helpers/dbHelper.js's header comment for the full rationale.
    beforeAll(async () => {
      const redis = getRedis();
      await redis.flushdb();
    });
    
    afterAll(async () => {
      const redis = getRedis();
      await redis.flushdb();
      await redis.quit();
    });
    
    afterEach(() => {
      jest.clearAllMocks();
    });
    
    // Generous default timeout bump is already set via the Jest project's
    // testTimeout: 30000 (package.test.json) — not repeated here.

      if (!parsed.success) throw new ValidationError('Invalid dispute arguments', null, parsed.error.issues);
      const { page, perPage, offset } = getPagination(parsed.data);
      const parameters = { workspaceId: context.workspace.id, statusFilter: parsed.data.status, page, perPage, offset, metadataOnly: true };
      const baseCurrency = context.workspace.baseCurrency;
      const disputeService = require('../../services/dispute.service');
      const { disputes, count } = await disputeService.listDisputes(parameters);
      return { disputes: disputes.map((dispute) => fieldsFrom(dispute, LIST_FIELDS)), base_currency: baseCurrency, pagination: pageMeta(count, page, perPage) };
    }
    
    async function getDispute({ context, args }) {
      assertAgentContext(context);
      const parsed = getDisputeArgsSchema.safeParse(args);
      if (!parsed.success) throw new ValidationError('Invalid dispute arguments', null, parsed.error.issues);
      const { page, perPage, offset } = getPagination(parsed.data);
      const workspaceId = context.workspace.id;
      const callerId = context.member.id;
      const isAdmin = context.member.role === 'admin';
      const baseCurrency = context.workspace.baseCurrency;
      const disputeService = require('../../services/dispute.service');
      const { dispute, entry, notesCount } = await disputeService.getDispute({
        workspaceId, disputeId: parsed.data.dispute_id, isAdmin, callerId, notesPagination: { page, perPage, offset },
      });
      if (!isAdmin && dispute.raised_by !== callerId) throw new ForbiddenError('You can only view disputes you raised');
      return {
        dispute: { ...fieldsFrom(dispute, DISPUTE_FIELDS), notes: dispute.notes.map((note) => fieldsFrom(note, ['author_id', 'note', 'added_at'])) },
        entry: entry ? fieldsFrom(entry, ENTRY_FIELDS) : null,
        base_currency: baseCurrency, notes_pagination: pageMeta(notesCount, page, perPage),
      };
    }
    
    module.exports = { listDisputes, getDispute };
    
    const { ValidationError } = require('../../utils/errors');
    const { getPagination, getPaginationMeta } = require('../../utils/pagination');
    const { assertAgentContext } = require('./context.service');
    const { listGroupsArgsSchema, getGroupArgsSchema, MAX_GROUP_PAGE } = require('../validators/group-tools.validator');
    
    const GROUP_FIELDS = Object.freeze(['id', 'name', 'description', 'created_at', 'updated_at']);
    const MEMBER_FIELDS = Object.freeze([
      'id', 'display_name', 'role', 'is_proxy', 'is_active', 'relationship_to_head', 'relationship_category', 'added_at',
    ]);
    const fieldsFrom = (row, fields) => Object.fromEntries(fields.map((field) => [field, row[field]]));
    function pageMeta(count, page, perPage) {
      const pagination = getPaginationMeta({ total: count, page, perPage });
      return { ...pagination, next_page: page < pagination.total_pages && page < MAX_GROUP_PAGE ? page + 1 : null };
    }
    
    async function listGroups({ context, args }) {
      assertAgentContext(context);
      const parsed = listGroupsArgsSchema.safeParse(args);
      if (!parsed.success) throw new ValidationError('Invalid group arguments', null, parsed.error.issues);
      const { page, perPage, offset } = getPagination(parsed.data);
      const parameters = {
        workspaceId: context.workspace.id, search: parsed.data.search, pagination: { page, perPage, offset },
      };
      const groupService = require('../../services/group.service');
      const { groups, count } = await groupService.listGroups(parameters);
      return { groups: groups.map((group) => fieldsFrom(group, GROUP_FIELDS)), pagination: pageMeta(count, page, perPage) };
    }
    
    async function getGroup({ context, args }) {
      // Unlike group browsing, the HTTP group-detail route is admin-only.
      assertAgentContext(context, 'admin');
      const parsed = getGroupArgsSchema.safeParse(args);
      if (!parsed.success) throw new ValidationError('Invalid group arguments', null, parsed.error.issues);
      const { page, perPage, offset } = getPagination(parsed.data);
      const parameters = {
        workspaceId: context.workspace.id, groupId: parsed.data.group_id, pagination: { page, perPage, offset },
      };
      const groupService = require('../../services/group.service');
      const { group, members, count } = await groupService.getGroup(parameters);
      return {
        group: fieldsFrom(group, GROUP_FIELDS), members: members.map((member) => fieldsFrom(member, MEMBER_FIELDS)),
        pagination: pageMeta(count, page, perPage),
      };
    }
    
    module.exports = { listGroups, getGroup };

    -- Kith — Database Schema
    -- A shared workspace for families/groups to coordinate money pooling,
    -- recurring contributions, tasks, milestones, and notifications.
    -- =====================================================================
    
    CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS public;
    
    -- Supabase normally installs extensions here. Including public also supports
    -- an existing pg_trgm installation there without moving the extension.
    CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS extensions;
    CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm WITH SCHEMA extensions;
    SET search_path TO public, extensions;
    
    SET default_tablespace = '';
    SET default_table_access_method = heap;

    // additions in 001_schema.sql. Unit mocks cannot verify SQL visibility or ranking.
    const { randomUUID } = require('crypto');
    const { supabaseAdmin } = require('../../../src/config/supabase');
    const { containsPattern } = require('../../../src/utils/ilike');
    const { seedWorkspaceWithAdmin, seedAdditionalMember, cleanupWorkspace } = require('../../helpers/dbHelper');
    const { buildContainer, buildTask, buildLedgerEntry, buildDispute, buildGroup } = require('../../fixtures/factories');
    
    const workspaceIds = [];
    async function insert(table, row) {
      const { data, error } = await supabaseAdmin.from(table).insert(row).select().single();
      if (error) throw error;
      return data;
    }
    async function update(table, id, data) {
      const { error } = await supabaseAdmin.from(table).update(data).eq('id', id);
      if (error) throw error;
    }
    async function seedTenant(displayName = 'Zinnia') {
      const tenant = await seedWorkspaceWithAdmin(supabaseAdmin, { member: { display_name: 'Xylophone' } });
      workspaceIds.push(tenant.workspace.id);
      const { member: caller } = await seedAdditionalMember(supabaseAdmin, tenant.workspace.id, { member: { display_name: displayName } });
      const container = await insert('containers', buildContainer({
        workspace_id: tenant.workspace.id, created_by: tenant.member.id, name: 'General',
      }));
      return { ...tenant, caller, container };
    }
    const addTask = (tenant, title, overrides = {}) => insert('container_tasks', buildTask({
      container_id: tenant.container.id, created_by: tenant.member.id, assigned_to: tenant.caller.id, title, ...overrides,
    }));
    const addEntry = (tenant, note, overrides = {}) => insert('ledger_entries', buildLedgerEntry({
      workspace_id: tenant.workspace.id, container_id: tenant.container.id,
      contributor_id: tenant.caller.id, recorded_by: tenant.member.id, note, ...overrides,
    }));
    async function addDispute(tenant, reason, overrides = {}) {
      const entryId = overrides.ledger_entry_id || (await addEntry(tenant, 'Unrelated', {
        status: 'confirmed', confirmed_by: tenant.member.id, confirmed_at: new Date().toISOString(),
      })).id;
      return insert('disputes', buildDispute({
        workspace_id: tenant.workspace.id, ledger_entry_id: entryId, raised_by: tenant.caller.id, reason, ...overrides,
      }));
    }
    const addGroup = (tenant, name, overrides = {}) => insert('groups', buildGroup({
      workspace_id: tenant.workspace.id, created_by: tenant.member.id, name, ...overrides,
    }));
    const definitions = [
      { label: 'tasks', rpc: 'search_tasks_ranked', create: addTask, ownerKey: 'assigned_to', containerFilter: true },
      { label: 'ledger entries', rpc: 'search_ledger_entries_ranked', create: addEntry, ownerKey: 'contributor_id', containerFilter: true },
      { label: 'disputes', rpc: 'search_disputes_ranked', create: addDispute, ownerKey: 'raised_by' },
      { label: 'groups', rpc: 'search_groups_ranked', create: addGroup },
    ];
    async function search(definition, tenant, {
      query = 'Rent', limit = 11, callerId = tenant.caller.id, isAdmin = false, containerId = null,
    } = {}) {
      const { data, error } = await supabaseAdmin.rpc(definition.rpc, {
        p_workspace_id: tenant.workspace.id, p_query: query, p_pattern: containsPattern(query), p_limit: limit,
        ...(definition.ownerKey ? { p_caller_id: callerId, p_is_admin: isAdmin } : {}),
        ...(definition.containerFilter ? { p_container_id: containerId } : {}),
      });
      if (error) throw error;
      return data;
    }
    const ids = (rows) => rows.map((row) => row.id).sort();
    
    afterAll(async () => {
      for (const workspaceId of workspaceIds.reverse()) await cleanupWorkspace(supabaseAdmin, workspaceId);
    });
    
    describe.each(definitions)('ranked $label SQL', (definition) => {
      it('ranks exact text before literal substrings and typos', async () => {
        const tenant = await seedTenant();
        const fuzzy = await definition.create(tenant, 'Adaze');
        const substring = await definition.create(tenant, 'Adaeze Okafor');
        const exact = await definition.create(tenant, 'Adaeze');
        const result = await search(definition, tenant, { query: 'adaeze' });
        expect(result.map((row) => row.id)).toEqual([exact.id, substring.id, fuzzy.id]);
        expect(result.map((row) => row.match_type)).toEqual(['exact', 'substring', 'fuzzy']);
        expect(result[2].score).toBeGreaterThan(0.3);
        expect(result[2].score).toBeLessThan(1);
      });
    
      it.each(['%_', '\\_'])('treats short wildcard characters literally: %s', async (query) => {
        const tenant = await seedTenant();
        const literal = await definition.create(tenant, `Literal ${query} text`);
        await definition.create(tenant, 'Unrelated');
        expect(ids(await search(definition, tenant, { query }))).toEqual([literal.id]);
      });
    
      it('preserves deterministic ID ordering and caps even a large requested limit', async () => {
        const tenant = await seedTenant();
        const rows = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < 23; i += 1) rows.push(await definition.create(tenant, 'Rent'));
        const expected = ids(rows);
        const bounded = await search(definition, tenant, { limit: 999 });
        expect(bounded.map((row) => row.id)).toEqual(expected.slice(0, 21));
        expect((await search(definition, tenant, { limit: 2 })).map((row) => row.id)).toEqual(expected.slice(0, 2));
        expect((await search(definition, tenant, { limit: 1 })).map((row) => row.id)).toEqual(expected.slice(0, 2));
      });
    
      it('excludes other workspaces, unmatched text and deleted workspaces', async () => {
        const tenant = await seedTenant();
        const other = await seedTenant();
        const visible = await definition.create(tenant, 'Rent');
        await definition.create(other, 'Rent');
        expect(ids(await search(definition, tenant, { callerId: tenant.member.id, isAdmin: true }))).toEqual([visible.id]);
        expect(await search(definition, tenant, { query: 'Zqvjkx' })).toEqual([]);
        await update('workspaces', tenant.workspace.id, { deleted_at: new Date().toISOString() });
        expect(await search(definition, tenant, { callerId: tenant.member.id, isAdmin: true })).toEqual([]);
      });
    
      it('rejects short or oversized queries in SQL even if the service validation was skipped', async () => {
        const tenant = await seedTenant();
        await definition.create(tenant, 'Rent');
        for (const query of ['', 'R', '9'.repeat(201)]) {
          expect(await search(definition, tenant, { query })).toEqual([]);
        }
      });
    });
    
    describe.each(definitions.filter((definition) => definition.ownerKey))('$label ownership in SQL', (definition) => {
      it('limits members to their own records and requires both admin sources for broader visibility', async () => {
        const tenant = await seedTenant();
        const own = await definition.create(tenant, 'Rent');
        const other = await definition.create(tenant, 'Rent', { [definition.ownerKey]: tenant.member.id });
        const all = [own, other];
        if (definition.containerFilter) all.push(await definition.create(tenant, 'Rent', { [definition.ownerKey]: null }));
        expect(ids(await search(definition, tenant))).toEqual([own.id]);
        // A stale or forged admin flag must not promote an actual member.
        expect(ids(await search(definition, tenant, { isAdmin: true }))).toEqual([own.id]);
        expect(ids(await search(definition, tenant, { callerId: tenant.member.id, isAdmin: true }))).toEqual(ids(all));
        expect(ids(await search(definition, tenant, { callerId: tenant.member.id, isAdmin: false }))).toEqual([other.id]);
      });
    
      it('requires a current membership in the requested workspace, including for claimed admins', async () => {
        const tenant = await seedTenant();
        const other = await seedTenant();
        await definition.create(tenant, 'Rent');
        for (const callerId of [null, randomUUID(), other.member.id]) {
          expect(await search(definition, tenant, { callerId, isAdmin: true })).toEqual([]);
        }
        await update('workspace_members', tenant.caller.id, { role: 'admin', is_active: false });
        expect(await search(definition, tenant, { isAdmin: true })).toEqual([]);
        await update('workspace_members', tenant.caller.id, { is_active: true, deleted_at: new Date().toISOString() });
        expect(await search(definition, tenant, { isAdmin: true })).toEqual([]);
      });
    });
    
    describe.each(definitions.filter((definition) => definition.containerFilter))('$label container boundaries', (definition) => {
      it('honors container filters without allowing a foreign or deleted parent', async () => {
        const tenant = await seedTenant();
        const foreign = await seedTenant();
        const secondContainer = await insert('containers', buildContainer({ workspace_id: tenant.workspace.id, created_by: tenant.member.id }));
        const first = await definition.create(tenant, 'Rent');
        const second = await definition.create(tenant, 'Rent', { container_id: secondContainer.id });
        await definition.create(foreign, 'Rent', { [definition.ownerKey]: tenant.caller.id });
        expect(ids(await search(definition, tenant))).toEqual(ids([first, second]));
        expect(ids(await search(definition, tenant, { containerId: secondContainer.id }))).toEqual([second.id]);
        expect(await search(definition, tenant, { containerId: foreign.container.id, isAdmin: true, callerId: tenant.member.id })).toEqual([]);
        await update('containers', tenant.container.id, { deleted_at: new Date().toISOString() });
        expect(ids(await search(definition, tenant))).toEqual([second.id]);
        expect(await search(definition, tenant, { containerId: tenant.container.id })).toEqual([]);
      });
    });
    
    it('excludes soft-deleted tasks even for admins', async () => {
      const tenant = await seedTenant();
      await addTask(tenant, 'Rent', { deleted_at: new Date().toISOString() });
      expect(await search(definitions[0], tenant, { callerId: tenant.member.id, isAdmin: true })).toEqual([]);
    });
    
    it('matches ledger notes and contributor names without exposing joined private fields', async () => {
      const tenant = await seedTenant('Adaeze Okafor');
      const entry = await addEntry(tenant, 'House repairs', { proofs: [{ url: 'PRIVATE_FILE' }] });
      const result = await search(definitions[1], tenant, { query: 'Adaze' });
      expect(result).toEqual([expect.objectContaining({ id: entry.id, contributor_name: 'Adaeze Okafor', match_type: 'fuzzy' })]);
      expect(ids(await search(definitions[1], tenant, { query: 'House repairs' }))).toEqual([entry.id]);
      expect(result[0]).not.toHaveProperty('proofs');
      expect(result[0]).not.toHaveProperty('base_amount');
      expect(result[0]).not.toHaveProperty('recorded_by');
    });
    
    it('matches exact original decimals in SQL and retains separate currencies and signed corrections', async () => {
      const tenant = await seedTenant();
      const ngn = await addEntry(tenant, null, { original_amount: '5000.10', original_currency: 'NGN' });
      const usd = await addEntry(tenant, null, { original_amount: '5000.10', original_currency: 'USD' });
      await addEntry(tenant, null, { original_amount: '5000.11' });
      const large = await addEntry(tenant, null, { original_amount: '9999999999999.99' });
      const negative = await addEntry(tenant, null, { original_amount: '-0.01', entry_type: 'correction', corrects_entry_id: ngn.id });
      const result = await search(definitions[1], tenant, { query: '+5000.1' });
      expect(ids(result)).toEqual(ids([ngn, usd]));
      expect(result.map((row) => row.original_currency).sort()).toEqual(['NGN', 'USD']);
      result.forEach((row) => expect(row).toMatchObject({ original_amount: '5000.10', match_type: 'exact' }));
      expect(await search(definitions[1], tenant, { query: '9999999999999.99' }))
        .toEqual([expect.objectContaining({ id: large.id, original_amount: '9999999999999.99' })]);
      expect(await search(definitions[1], tenant, { query: '-0.01' }))
        .toEqual([expect.objectContaining({ id: negative.id, original_amount: '-0.01', entry_type: 'correction' })]);
      for (const query of ['5,000.10', '5e3', '5000.100', '999999999999999999999999999999.99']) {
        expect(await search(definitions[1], tenant, { query })).toEqual([]);
      }
    });
    
    it('requires both ledger and container workspace IDs and scopes contributor joins', async () => {
      const tenant = await seedTenant();
      const foreign = await seedTenant('Quetzalforeign');
      await addEntry(tenant, 'Rent', { container_id: foreign.container.id });
      await addEntry(tenant, 'Rent', { workspace_id: foreign.workspace.id });
      const visible = await addEntry(tenant, 'Rent', { contributor_id: foreign.caller.id });
      const result = await search(definitions[1], tenant, { callerId: tenant.member.id, isAdmin: true });
      expect(result).toEqual([expect.objectContaining({ id: visible.id, contributor_name: null })]);
      expect(await search(definitions[1], tenant, { query: 'Quetzalforeign', callerId: tenant.member.id, isAdmin: true })).toEqual([]);
    });
    
    it('finds historical disputes by raiser or ledger note even after their container is deleted', async () => {
      const tenant = await seedTenant('Adaeze Okafor');
      const entry = await addEntry(tenant, 'Receipt reference');
      const dispute = await addDispute(tenant, 'Wrong amount', { ledger_entry_id: entry.id, notes: [{ note: 'PRIVATE_NOTE' }] });
      await update('containers', tenant.container.id, { deleted_at: new Date().toISOString() });
      const result = await search(definitions[2], tenant, { query: 'Receipt reference' });
      expect(result).toEqual([expect.objectContaining({ id: dispute.id, ledger_entry_id: entry.id, match_type: 'exact' })]);
      expect(result[0]).not.toHaveProperty('notes');
      expect(result[0]).not.toHaveProperty('note');
      expect(ids(await search(definitions[2], tenant, { query: 'Adaze' }))).toEqual([dispute.id]);
    });
    
    it('does not match dispute candidates through foreign member names or ledger notes', async () => {
      const tenant = await seedTenant();
      const foreign = await seedTenant('Quetzalforeign');
      const entry = await addEntry(foreign, 'Privatereceipt');
      const dispute = await addDispute(tenant, 'Localreason', { raised_by: foreign.caller.id, ledger_entry_id: entry.id });
      const asAdmin = { callerId: tenant.member.id, isAdmin: true };
      expect(await search(definitions[2], tenant, { ...asAdmin, query: 'Localreason' }))
        .toEqual([expect.objectContaining({ id: dispute.id, raised_by_name: null })]);
      expect(await search(definitions[2], tenant, { ...asAdmin, query: 'Quetzalforeign' })).toEqual([]);
      expect(await search(definitions[2], tenant, { ...asAdmin, query: 'Privatereceipt' })).toEqual([]);
    });

    ## Notification reads
    
    `list_notifications` and `get_unread_count` read only the caller's own inbox
    in the authenticated workspace, including for admins. Both handlers check
    membership, reject recipient/workspace overrides, and wrap the existing
    notification inbox service. Listing accepts optional boolean `is_read`,
    `page` (1–10,000), and `per_page` (1–100). Counting accepts only `{}`.
    
    Lists return permitted notification text/reference fields and read timestamps,
    omitting delivery internals and deduplication keys. Results include filtered
    pagination with `next_page`; `unread_count` covers all unread notifications in
    this workspace, independent of the list filter or page. Reading does not mark
    anything as read. Notification titles/bodies remain untrusted tool content.
    
    The inbox service now applies the same recipient/workspace scope to the list
    and unread counter, uses stable creation-date/ID ordering, and rejects query
    failures or unavailable counts with `NOTIFICATIONS_UNAVAILABLE`. Existing
    HTTP read controllers use the workspace from the resolved membership and
    keep their existing response envelopes. Mocked service, tool, loop, and HTTP
    tests cover these boundaries; live database/model verification remains pending.
    
    ## Group reads
    
    `list_groups({ search?, page?, per_page? })` is a Tier 1 read available to
    members and admins. It returns group metadata (ID, name, description and
    timestamps) and an exact filtered group count. Search is an escaped literal
    name substring, 2–200 characters; it does not resolve spelling errors. Groups
    are ordered by name then ID. Embedded memberships and membership counts are
    omitted from this list.
    
    `get_group({ group_id, page?, per_page? })` is **admin-only**, matching the
    existing group-detail HTTP route. It returns group metadata, a bounded page
    of membership directory fields and an exact membership count. Both the group
    and the joined memberships are scoped to the authenticated workspace. Deleted
    members are excluded; proxies and inactive memberships remain visible.
    Members are ordered by added timestamp then group-membership ID. No contact
    information, actor IDs, or financial details are exposed.
    
    Both tools use pages 1–10,000 and 1–100 rows per page (defaults 1/20), with
    `pagination.next_page` null at the last page or page limit. Group detail

    +places. SQL compares them as `numeric` and returns original amounts as decimal
    +text, preserving precision and each entry's currency. For a one-digit amount,

    +commas, scientific notation and natural-language amounts are not interpreted
    +as amounts. This search does not convert currencies, infer dates or calculate
    +totals; the same amount in different currencies can yield separate candidates.

    indexes, and ranked-search RPCs for members, containers, tasks, ledger entries,
    disputes and groups. Existing `pg_trgm` installations in either `public` or
    `extensions` are supported. The RPCs receive the escaped pattern from the
    shared `containsPattern` helper.
    
    For an existing database, apply only these additions, with function creation
    and permission changes in the same transaction; do not replay the consolidated
    schema against existing tables. RPC execution is revoked from PUBLIC and
    Supabase browser roles and granted to `service_role` when present. Schema edits
    in the repository do not update a running database or its PostgREST schema cache.
    Reload that cache after applying the additions and before exercising the tools.
    
    Run `npm run test:unit -- --runInBand` from `backend`. Real trigram ranking,
